606-of-satania.name: 606 de Satania
606-of-satania.meaning: The number of Urantia as the 606th inhabited world registered in the local system of Satania (43:0.1, 49:0.3).

abel.name: Abel
abel.meaning: The first child of Adam and Eve born in the second garden, a herder (76:2.1).

abner.name: Abner
abner.meaning: The chief of the disciples of John the Baptist, later head of the seventy messengers and leader of the church at Philadelphia (Papers 163, 166, 171).

aborigines-australian.name: aborígenes (australianos)
aborigines-australian.meaning: The natives of Australia, cited as survivors of primitive, antisocial social conditions (68:1.6).

abraham-old-testament.name: Abraham (Antiguo Testamento)
abraham-old-testament.meaning: The Hebrew patriarch who became the pupil of Melchizedek and an ancestor of Joseph (93:5.1).

absolute.name: Absoluto
absolute.meaning: The one Absolute of infinity (three Absolutes on subinfinite levels), conceived as the impersonal reaction of the Trinity; also the Buddhist concept of the Eternal One (56:9.5, Paper 94).

rejected.reason: The neuter article makes it an abstract quality; the papers treat it as a reality parallel to 'the Trinity' (56:9.5).

absolute-buddha.name: Buda Absoluto
absolute-buddha.meaning: The Buddhist concept of the Buddha as the Eternal One of infinite existence, the Buddhist approach to Deity (Paper 94).

rejected.reason: 'Buda' is the standard Spanish form of the historical name (rule 2).

absolute-deity.name: Deidad Absoluta
absolute-deity.meaning: Deity on the absolute level; the absolute aspect of Deity, distinct from the Deity Absolute (0:1.13, 56:9).

rejected.reason: That is the form of 'Deity Absolute'; the order of the English words marks two terms.

absolute-mind-person.name: Mente Absoluta (persona)
absolute-mind-person.meaning: The Infinite Spirit as the personalization of absolute mind (3:1.8, 9:7.4).

rejected.reason: 'Intelecto' would break the 'mind = mente' family.

absolute-person.name: Persona Absoluta
absolute-person.meaning: The Eternal Son, the absolute personality, though not in the experiential sense the personalization of the Absolute (0:5.5, 56:9.5).

rejected.reason: 'Personality' and 'person' are different English words; 0:5.5 uses 'absolute personality' separately.

absolutes.name: Absolutos
absolutes.meaning: The seven Absolutes of Infinity, the eternal and co-ordinate premises of all reality (Father, Son, Spirit, Paradise, and the three potential Absolutes); 'three absolute actuals' names the Father, Son, and Spirit or the actual side against the three potential Absolutes (Paper 105, 0:11).

rejected.reason: False friend: Spanish 'actual' means 'current, present-day'.
'Actualizado' commonly means 'updated'.
'Real' also means 'royal', and as a noun a coin.

absoniters.name: absonitarios
absoniters.meaning: Beings of the absonite level, not created but eventuated (0:1.12).

rejected.reason: The same form as the adjective "absonito"; "-ario" follows "finaliters: finalitarios".
Says they make things absonite.

absonity.name: absonidad
absonity.meaning: The quality or level of the absonite, between finite and absolute, which Paradise arrivals study after divinity (0:9.2, 30:4.31).

rejected.reason: Less natural; "-idad" matches "divinity: divinidad".

actual.name: actual
actual.meaning: That which exists in fullness of expression, in contrast to the potential, which carries undisclosed capacity for growth (0:4.7, 115:3.16).

rejected.reason: Collides with 'realidad' (reality), of which the actual is only one phase (0:4.1, 0:4.7).
Breaks the family with 'actualizar' and also means 'cash'.
The reader must not bring 'current, present-day'. The sense is 'existing in act'.

actual.note: The packet names 'actual' as a false friend. I keep it only because the papers set 'actual' against 'potential' in a philosophical sense, which Spanish philosophy writes as 'actual / en acto'. A human must decide if readers will take it as 'current'.

actual-the.name: Actual, lo
actual-the.meaning: The triodity of actuality: the union of the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and the Paradise Isle, which is the actual revelation of the originality of the First Source and Center (115:3.7).

rejected.reason: Masculine article reads as a person; the English names a union of three, so the neuter 'lo' fits.
Collides with 'realidad' (reality).

actual-the.note: Same false-friend risk as 'actual': 'lo actual' reads as 'what is current'. The capital helps, but a human must check it.
forcedChoices: Spanish needs an article; I chose the neuter 'lo', which the context (a union, not a person) supports.

adam.name: Adán
adam.meaning: The Material Son sent with Eve to Urantia as a biologic uplifter (51:0.1).

adamites.name: Adamitas
adamites.meaning: The violet race, the descendants of Adam and Eve on Urantia, who mixed with the evolutionary races to uplift them biologically.

rejected.reason: Possible adjective, but the noun form parallels 'Anditas' and 'Andonitas' already chosen.

adamson.name: Adamson
adamson.meaning: The first-born son of Adam and Eve, who with Ratta founded a center north of the second garden and became an origin of the secondary midwayers (77:5.6, 80:7.3).

rejected.reason: The name exists only in this book, so the English spelling stays; a translation hides that it is a name.

adamson.note: Adam is "Adán" in Spanish, so a reviewer can choose to keep "Adamson" (book-only name, rule 3) or adapt it. I keep it.

adamsonites.name: Adamsonitas
adamsonites.meaning: The descendants of Adamson and Ratta, who kept a high culture for almost seven thousand years at their center east of the Caspian Sea (77:5.9, 78:1.3).

adjuster-expression.name: expresión del Ajustador
adjuster-expression.meaning: The expression of the indwelling Adjuster through the mortal mind and personality (Paper 110).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish; the hyphen compound does not exist.

adjuster-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Ajustador
adjuster-fused-mortals.meaning: Ascending mortals whose souls have fused with their indwelling Thought Adjuster; one of three orders of fusion (40:9.1, 40:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'Fundido' also means 'melted' or 'burnt out'.

adjuster-fusion.name: fusión con el Ajustador
adjuster-fusion.meaning: The eternal union of the surviving mortal soul with the indwelling Thought Adjuster (40:9.1, Paper 110).

rejected.reason: Reads as the Adjuster fusing with something else by itself.

adjutant-mind-spirits.name: espíritus ayudantes de la mente
adjutant-mind-spirits.meaning: Seven spirits, children of the Universe Mother Spirit, that minister mind to the lower orders of intelligent life and condition organic evolution (36:5.1, 101:5.10).

rejected.reason: A calque; the hyphen compound is not natural in Spanish.
'Adjunto' means attached or an assistant rank; less clear than 'ayudante'.

rejected.form: espíritu de valor (for spirit of courage)
rejected.reason: 'Valor' also means 'value', a frequent term in the papers; 'coraje' has one sense.

rejected.form: espíritu de culto (for spirit of worship)
rejected.reason: 'Culto' is ritual or a sect; 'adoración' is the act of worship.

administrator-seraphim.name: serafines administradores
administrator-seraphim.meaning: The fourth order of seraphim, who serve the administration of the local systems (39:4.1).

africa.name: África
africa.meaning: The continent to which the indigo race and other Sangik peoples migrated, and where the indigo race remained (64:6).

agni.name: Agni
agni.meaning: The three-headed Aryan fire god, lord of the earth and a remnant of an earlier Trinity concept, sometimes exalted as head of the Vedic pantheon (94:1.3, 94:1.4).

ahab.name: Acab
ahab.meaning: A Hebrew king whom Elijah denounced for the murder of the Naboths to take their land (97:3.6, 97:9.19).

alaska.name: Alaska
alaska.meaning: The northwest region of North America, named in the papers for its rock ridges and ancient volcanoes (58:7.4, 59:5.20).

alexander-the-great.name: Alejandro Magno
alexander-the-great.meaning: The Macedonian king who expanded Greece into an empire from the Adriatic to the Indus and spread Hellenistic civilization (195:1.7).

alexandria.name: Alejandría
alexandria.meaning: The Egyptian city of the great library, where Jesus lived as a child and later visited (Papers 122-123, 130).

almighty-supreme.name: Supremo Todopoderoso
almighty-supreme.meaning: The power aspect of the Supreme Being, the experiential power of God the Supreme that synthesizes in the grand universe (0:7.7).

rejected.reason: Order makes 'Todopoderoso' the name; in English 'Supreme' is the head noun.
Plainer Spanish is 'Todopoderoso'.

alpheus-twins.name: gemelos Alfeo
alpheus-twins.meaning: James and Judas Alpheus, twin fishermen who were two of the twelve apostles of Jesus (Paper 139:10).

rejected.reason: Alpheus is a biblical name with a standard Spanish form.

alps.name: Alpes
alps.meaning: The European mountain range, used as a measure of height (59:1.8).

amadon.name: Amadon
amadon.meaning: The Andonite associate of Van who stayed loyal in the Lucifer rebellion and gave his name to the 144 loyal Amadonites (67:6.3).

amadonites.name: Amadonitas
amadonites.meaning: The descendants of the Andonites who stayed loyal with Van and Amadon; a cultural and religious name more than a racial one (73:1.3, 67:6.2).

amathus.name: Amatus
amathus.meaning: A town east of the Jordan, on the east Jordan road that Jesus took back to Nazareth (128:1.14).

rejected.reason: The Spanish name of a different Amathus, the city in Cyprus.
Keeps the English-Latin spelling with 'th', which Spanish does not use.

amathus.note: I do not know an established Spanish form for this Perean town. A human must confirm 'Amatus' or choose another form.

amenemope.name: Amenemope
amenemope.meaning: An Egyptian teacher whose Book of Wisdom passed almost word for word into Hebrew Proverbs (95:4.5).

amos-prophet.name: Amós (profeta)
amos-prophet.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who proclaimed Yahweh the 'God of all nations' and was stoned to death (97:4.4).

ancients-of-days.name: Ancianos de Días
ancients-of-days.meaning: The Trinity-origin rulers of the superuniverses, three on each capital, whom ascenders meet in the superuniverse (18:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Antiguo' describes old things or former holders of a role, not an elder person.
The extra article is not in the English and makes it less like a title.

ancients-of-days-of-uversa.name: Ancianos de Días de Uversa
ancients-of-days-of-uversa.meaning: The three Trinity-origin rulers of Orvonton on Uversa, who confirm rulings of the Most Highs (93:10.6).

andites.name: Anditas
andites.meaning: The best all-round human stock since the violet race, a blend of Adamite and Nodite remnants with the best of other races (78:4.3, 80:4.5).

andon-and-fonta.name: Andon y Fonta
andon-and-fonta.meaning: The first two human beings on Urantia, the parents of mankind (Paper 63).

rejected.reason: These names exist only in this book; the rule keeps the English spelling. 'Andonitas' keeps the same root.

andonites.name: Andonitas
andonites.meaning: The first human race, descendants of Andon and Fonta, swarthy hunters who resembled the present-day Eskimo (63:4.1, 63:5.6).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes peoples in lowercase, but this name exists only in this book and the packet keeps English capitals on coined terms.

andrew.name: Andrés
andrew.meaning: Andrew, brother of Peter, the first apostle and chairman of the twelve (139:1.1).

andronover.name: Andronover
andronover.meaning: The former spiral nebula whose center is the nucleus of the physical system to which our sun belongs (15:3.6, 57:3.2).

angels.name: ángeles
angels.meaning: The ministering spirits, the angelic hosts born of the Infinite Spirit and its associated creative Spirits (17:8.2).

angona.name: Angona
angona.meaning: The dark giant system whose near approach drew from the sun the matter that became the solar system (57:5.6, 57:5.13).

annas.name: Anás
annas.meaning: The former Jewish high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas, who knew Jesus earlier and held the preliminary examination of Jesus (142:0.2, 183:5.1).

antarctica.name: Antártida
antarctica.meaning: The southern continent, which rose with the other land masses from the Pacific depths (57:8.21).

antioch.name: Antioquía
antioch.meaning: The city of Syria where Jesus lived for over two months on his Mediterranean journey and where Paul later preached (134:7.3).

rejected.reason: Without the accent it is the Colombian department; the ancient city is Antioquía.

apostles-of-jesus.name: apóstoles de Jesús
apostles-of-jesus.meaning: The twelve men Jesus chose as his personal companions and ambassadors of the kingdom (138:0.1, 139:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Ignorante' adds an insult; 'iletrado' keeps the sense of no formal schooling.

apostles-of-john-the-baptist.name: apóstoles de Juan el Bautista
apostles-of-john-the-baptist.meaning: The twelve leaders whom John the Baptist named as his apostles; they conferred and worked with Jesus' apostles (144:6.9, 150:5.1).

appalachian-mountains.name: montes Apalaches
appalachian-mountains.meaning: The mountain range of eastern North America, named for its rock layers and for arctic species left on its peaks after the last ice age (59:4.16, 61:7.16).

arabia.name: Arabia
arabia.meaning: The desert peninsula where the Salem missionaries failed through overorganization and where clans kept a hazy idea of one God (95:7.1, 95:7.3).

archangels.name: arcángeles
archangels.meaning: Offspring of the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit who serve the resurrection and survival of creatures (37:3.1).

rejected.reason: the reader must not bring the seven named archangels of tradition; this is an order of the local universe

architects-of-the-master-universe.name: Arquitectos del Universo Maestro
architects-of-the-master-universe.meaning: The absonite planners of the master universe, 28,011 in number, organized by space levels (31:9.1).

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family

architectural-spheres.name: esferas arquitectónicas
architectural-spheres.meaning: Worlds made to order, such as Salvington, Edentia, and Jerusem, lighted and energized independently of the suns (41:1.3, 43:0.2).

rejected.reason: Not standard Spanish.

aryans.name: arios
aryans.meaning: The Andite invaders of India, whose racial effect was strong only in the northern provinces (79:4.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes peoples in lowercase.

aryans.note: 'ario' carries modern racist political senses in Spanish. The papers use it in a historical sense.

ascending-mortals.name: mortales ascendentes
aliases: mortales fusionados con el Ajustador en ascenso
ascending-mortals.meaning: Mortals who survive and progress from the material worlds through the mansion worlds, the superuniverse, and Havona to Paradise (49:0.1, 47:3.12, 53:3.6).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'ascendiente' means an ancestor or an influence.
Plain, but does not work as a noun phrase in all contexts; the English 'ascendant' and 'ascending' both go to 'ascendente'.

ascending-pilgrims.name: peregrinos ascendentes
ascending-pilgrims.meaning: Ascending creatures of time who pass through the Havona universe on their way to Paradise (13:1.21).

ascending-sons-of-god.name: hijos de Dios ascendentes
ascending-sons-of-god.meaning: Creatures of evolutionary origin who climb toward Paradise, helped by the descending Sons; translated midwayers are registered among them (20:1.1, 40:3.1).

ascendington.name: Ascendington
ascendington.meaning: The seventh sacred world of the Father around Paradise, the home and rendezvous of the ascending pilgrims during their Havona life (13:1.21, 13:1.23).

asia.name: Asia
asia.meaning: The continent that was the homeland of the human race and of the early civilizations (64:1.1, 78:1.1).

assigned-sentinels.name: Centinelas Asignados
assigned-sentinels.meaning: Co-ordinating personalities and liaison representatives of the Seven Supreme Executives, personalized by the Infinite Spirit, who serve in rotation on the system capitals (24:5.1, 24:5.3).

associate-circuit-supervisors.name: Supervisores Asociados de los Circuitos
associate-circuit-supervisors.meaning: The seven supervisors on the Paradise spheres of the Spirit who, with the Supreme Power Centers, co-ordinate the circuits that pass out to the seven superuniverses (24:1.8).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of the done 'Supervisores de los Circuitos del Universo'.

associate-inspectors.name: Inspectores Asociados
associate-inspectors.meaning: Higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit who represent the Seven Supreme Executives in the local universes, one on each local universe headquarters as a close associate of the Union of Days (24:4.2).

associate-power-directors.name: directores asociados del poder
associate-power-directors.meaning: The first group of Master Physical Controllers, who assign and dispatch all orders of physical controllers as the energy needs of the realms change (29:4.15, 29:4.18).

associate-transcendental-master-force-or.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Trascendentales Asociados
aliases: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Asociados
associate-transcendental-master-force-or.meaning: The second group of Master Force Organizers, whose pressure-presence and tension-trends bring space-energy from the puissant to the gravity stage (29:0.3, 42:2.12).

rejected.form: Organizadores Asociados Trascendentales Maestros de la Fuerza
rejected.reason: Splits "Maestros de la Fuerza" from "Organizadores"; the order follows "Controladores Físicos Maestros".

assyria.name: Asiria
assyria.meaning: The empire to which the northern kingdom refused tribute, after which Israel was besieged and dispersed (97:9.21).

athens.name: Atenas
athens.meaning: The Greek city where Paul spoke before the Areopagus about 'the Unknown God' (195:1.1).

attis.name: Atis
attis.meaning: The son of Cybele in the Phrygian mystery cult (98:4.3).

augustus.name: Augusto
augustus.meaning: The Roman emperor who died in A.D. 14, with Tiberius as coemperor before his death (136:2.8, 133:2.5).

australia.name: Australia
australia.meaning: The southern continent that split from the early land mass and evolved in isolation.

avalon.name: Avalon
avalon.meaning: One of the nearest local universes to Nebadon (32:2.12).

rejected.reason: The Spanish form of the island of Arthurian legend; that is not this universe.

avalon.note: A reader can link 'Avalon' to the Arthurian legend; the papers use it only as the name of a local universe.

avonals-order-of.name: Avonales, orden de los
avonals-order-of.meaning: The order of Paradise Sons also called Magisterial Sons (20:1.11, 20:6.5).

rejected.reason: Keep the name, but Spanish forms the plural of a noun in -al with -es.

baal.name: Baal
baal.meaning: The Canaanite god whose name means 'owner', a god of rain and of land ownership and fertility (97:3.3).

babel.name: Babel
babel.meaning: The city that grew from the planned center named Bablot, later Bablod, and finally Babel (77:3.3).

babylon.name: Babilonia
babylon.meaning: The Mesopotamian city of the temples of Bel-Marduk and of the Hebrew captivity (95:1.10).

babylonian-captivity.name: cautiverio babilónico
babylonian-captivity.meaning: The exile of the Jews in Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem, which turned them firmly to monotheism (97:9).

rejected.reason: 'cautividad' is correct but less common than 'cautiverio'.

badonan-tribes.name: tribus de Badonan
badonan-tribes.meaning: The descendants of Badonan in the highlands northwest of India who kept traditions of Andon and from whose improved stock the Neanderthal race came (64:2.4, 64:3.5).

rejected.reason: Makes an adjective the English does not use.

barabbas.name: Barrabás
barabbas.meaning: The murderer whom Pilate released instead of Jesus at the demand of the crowd (185:5.4).

beauty.name: belleza
beauty.meaning: With truth and goodness one of the three divine values; the harmony and unity of reality that creatures perceive and that leads to worship (2:7, 56:10).

rejected.reason: Mostly physical attractiveness; narrower.

beelzebub.name: Belcebú
beelzebub.meaning: The leader of the disloyal secondary midwayers who allied themselves with Caligastia (53:1.5, 77:7.4).

bering-strait-land-bridge.name: puente terrestre del estrecho de Bering
bering-strait-land-bridge.meaning: The land link between North America and Asia, over which the early lemurs and later peoples migrated (62:1.2).

bestowal.name: otorgamiento
bestowal.meaning: The act in which a Paradise Son gives himself to live as a creature (often as a mortal) on a world of his domain, and also any divine gift given (20:5.6, 20:6.5, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: Not every bestowal is in mortal flesh, and the English uses 'incarnate' as a separate word.
Ordinary sense is a donation of money or organs.
Not natural Spanish; the reflexive verb 'otorgarse' carries the self-giving.

forcedChoices: keep 'otorgamiento' from the done term 'Pentecostés (otorgamiento del Espíritu de la Verdad)': Rule 4: one English word, one Spanish word. Note that 'otorgamiento' has a legal or administrative ring in ordinary use; the reader must take it as self-giving.

bethany-beyond-jordan.name: Betania más allá del Jordán
aliases: Betania al otro lado del Jordán
bethany-beyond-jordan.meaning: The place across the Jordan where Jesus and the apostles stayed for some weeks of teaching (141:7.2).

bethany-near-jerusalem.name: Betania (cerca de Jerusalén)
bethany-near-jerusalem.meaning: The village near Jerusalem, home of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary, where Jesus first stayed with them in his youth (125:2.7).

bethlehem-judea.name: Belén (Judea)
bethlehem-judea.meaning: The town in Judea, the City of David, where Jesus was born.

bethsaida.name: Betsaida
bethsaida.meaning: The fishing harbor near Capernaum, home of several apostles and a center of Jesus' work (129:1.2, 150:1.1).

bethsaida-julias.name: Betsaida-Julias
bethsaida-julias.meaning: A city near the park where about five thousand gathered before the feeding (152:2.4, 157:2.1).

blue-race.name: raza azul
blue-race.meaning: One of the six colored Sangik races of Urantia, which spread in Europe and later mixed with the Andites and Adamites.

brahman.name: Brahman
brahman.meaning: The Hindu concept of the Absolute, the infinite IT IS, the Universal Self existing static and potential through all eternity, never conceived as a personality (94:3.3).

rejected.reason: The personal creator god of Hinduism, a different concept.

brahmanism.name: brahmanismo
brahmanism.meaning: The religious philosophy of India under the Brahman priests, which came near the idea of the indwelling Adjuster but held that no human individuality exists apart from the indwelling Universal One (94:3.6).

bright-and-morning-stars.name: Resplandecientes Estrellas Matutinas
bright-and-morning-stars.meaning: The first order of Universe Aids, one in each local universe, the first-born of its native creatures and its chief executive; Gabriel is the one of Nebadon (37:1.9).

rejected.reason: 'Brillantes' is already 'Brilliant' in 'Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas'; one English word has one translation.
Repeats 'Brillantes' and reads awkwardly.
A common name of the planet Venus, and of Lucifer in tradition.

forcedChoices: The English 'Bright and Morning' joins two qualifiers with 'and'; a literal 'y' reads awkwardly in Spanish, so both qualify 'Estrellas' without the conjunction, parallel to 'Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas'.

brilliant-evening-stars.name: Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas
brilliant-evening-stars.meaning: Superangels of the local universe who serve as liaison officers of Gabriel, some created and some ascendant (37:2.1).

rejected.reason: the ordinary name of the planet Venus
also reads as Venus

brilliant-evening-stars-chief.name: Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas (jefe)
aliases: jefe de las Brillantes Estrellas Vespertinas
brilliant-evening-stars-chief.meaning: The head of the Brilliant Evening Stars in the local universe, who has custody of and dispatches all personal communications (39:2.17).
forcedChoices: Spanish "jefe" is masculine; the English "chief" has no gender. I keep the masculine as the unmarked form.

british-isles.name: Islas Británicas
british-isles.meaning: The island group of northwestern Europe that includes Great Britain and Ireland (historical geography, standard Spanish form).

rejected.reason: Excludes Ireland; it is only the alias form.

broadcasters-superior-seraphim.name: difusores (serafines superiores)
broadcasters-superior-seraphim.meaning: Seraphic recorders among the superior seraphim who send out records and essential information (39:2.9).

rejected.reason: ties the term to radio technology
technical sense of a device or a currency issuer

broadcasts-celestial.name: difusiones (celestiales)
broadcasts-celestial.meaning: The communications sent from Paradise, the superuniverses, and the local universes, received on the capitals and displayed to all beings, such as the stream of space reports (44:4.9, 46:3.1).

rejected.reason: Correct, but 'broadcasters' is already 'difusores'; the family keeps one root.
Also means a release of money or of gases.

broadcasts-celestial.note: 'difusión' is also a general word for spreading news. The context shows a broadcast.

brotherhood-of-man.name: fraternidad de los hombres
brotherhood-of-man.meaning: The relationship of all persons as brothers that follows from the fatherhood of God, preached together with it in the gospel (193:0.4, 140:10.9).

rejected.reason: In Spanish the singular can read as the brotherhood of one man.
'Hermandad' also means a guild or confraternity; 'brotherhood' is already 'fraternidad' in 'espíritus de la fraternidad'.
Changes the noun 'man' to an adjective and loses 'el hombre'.

brotherhood-of-united-midwayers.name: Fraternidad de los Seres Intermedios Unidos
brotherhood-of-united-midwayers.meaning: The united corps of primary and secondary midwayers on Urantia, in whose name the narrator of the Jesus papers writes (121:8.14, 77:8.1).

rejected.form: Hermandad de los Seres Intermedios Unidos
rejected.reason: 'brotherhood' is already 'fraternidad' in 'espíritus de la fraternidad'; one word keeps one translation.

buddha.name: Buda
buddha.meaning: The title given to Gautama; Jesus said Buddha was better than Buddhism, a great man and prophet who lost sight of his spiritual Father (92:5.12, 132:7.4).

buddhism.name: budismo
buddhism.meaning: The religion that grew from the teachings of Gautama Buddha (94:8.1, 94:11.1).

bushmen.name: bosquimanos
bushmen.meaning: A small people of southern Africa with a primitive culture (66:5.30).

caesarea.name: Cesarea
caesarea.meaning: The coastal city built by Herod, the Roman capital of Palestine.

caesarea-philippi.name: Cesarea de Filipo
caesarea-philippi.meaning: The city in the north of Palestine where Jesus and the apostles stayed and taught for two weeks (155:2.1).

rejected.reason: Less usual than 'Cesarea de Filipo'.

caiaphas.name: Caifás
caiaphas.meaning: The acting high priest and son-in-law of Annas, before whom Jesus was tried (183:5.1).

cain.name: Caín
cain.meaning: The son of Eve who killed Abel, later repented and received an Adjuster (76:2.8).

california.name: California
california.meaning: The region on the western coast of North America.

caligastia.name: Caligastia
caligastia.meaning: The Planetary Prince of Urantia who joined the Lucifer rebellion and was deposed (67:6.5 context).

caligastia-one-hundred.name: cien de Caligastia
caligastia-one-hundred.meaning: The corporeal members of the Planetary Prince's staff, fifty men and fifty women, who came to Urantia in material bodies (66:2.3, 66:4.2).

rejected.reason: Is a military staff; the papers mean a corps of assistants and teachers.
The English writes 'one hundred' in lowercase.

cana.name: Caná
cana.meaning: The Galilean town where Jesus turned water into wine (138:8.5).

canada.name: Canadá
canada.meaning: The present North American country, where the oldest fossil-bearing rock layer comes to the surface (58:7.4).

cano.name: Cano
cano.meaning: The brilliant leader of the friendly Nodites near the Garden who met Eve in secret and believed in the Serapatatia plan (75:3.7, 75:3.8).
cano.note: Spanish "cano" is an adjective for gray hair. The capital marks the name, but a reader can notice the common word.

capernaum.name: Cafarnaúm
capernaum.meaning: The fishing town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee, Jesus' headquarters in his public work (Papers 129-150).

rejected.reason: Less common; 'Cafarnaúm' is the usual Spanish form.

caspian-sea.name: mar Caspio
caspian-sea.meaning: The inland sea whose southeastern region Jesus reached as conductor of a caravan from April A.D. 24 for a year (134:2.1).
caspian-sea.note: The packet summary gives the dates as 'April 24 to April 25 CE'; 134:2.1 says the trip began on April 1, A.D. 24, and lasted a full year.

celestial-artisans.name: artesanos celestiales
celestial-artisans.meaning: Recruited artists and artisans of the morontia and lower spirit realms, organized in seven divisions (Paper 44).

celestial-guardians.name: Guardianes Celestiales
celestial-guardians.meaning: Twice-trinitized sons, co-ordinates of the High Son Assistants, commissioned to the courts of the Ancients of Days (22:1.12).
celestial-guardians.note: "guardianes" is also used in "ángeles guardianes" and "guardianes del destino"; the capitals separate this order.

celestial-musicians.name: músicos celestiales
celestial-musicians.meaning: Celestial artisans who produce celestial harmony by the manipulation of spirit forces (44:1.2).

celestial-overseers.name: Superintendentes Celestiales
celestial-overseers.meaning: A recruited corps of over three million volunteers in Nebadon who serve as educational advisers and inspectors of the local universe school system (37:6.1, 30:2.146).

rejected.reason: "Supervisores" already renders "Supervisors" (Supreme Center Supervisors); one English word, one Spanish word.
The papers use "inspectors" as a description of their work (37:6.1), not as the name.
Archaic or regional in most countries.

celestial-recorders.name: Registradores Celestiales
celestial-recorders.meaning: Ascendant seraphim who make all superuniverse records in duplicate, a spirit original and a semimaterial copy (25:6.1, 25:6.5).

census-directors.name: Directores del Censo
census-directors.meaning: Higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit, with headquarters on the superuniverse capitals, who keep the record of will creatures (24:0.10, 24:2.3).

central-universe.name: universo central
central-universe.meaning: Havona, the eternal and perfect creation of a billion worlds around the Isle of Paradise (0:0.5).

chaldeans.name: caldeos
chaldeans.meaning: Eastern Semites near Ur, among the most advanced of them, and star worshipers who saw themselves as children of the sky father and the earth mother (96:2.1, 85:5.1).

chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.name: jazán de la sinagoga de Nazaret
chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.meaning: The officer of the synagogue who taught the children of Nazareth, Jesus' teacher (123:5.3, 123:5.5).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish has an adapted form.
The later sense of the word; here he is the teacher of the school.

chazan-of-nazareth-synagogue.note: In modern use the word means the cantor of the synagogue; the papers use the older sense of school officer.

cherubim-and-sanobim.name: querubines y sanobines
cherubim-and-sanobim.meaning: Paired assistants of the seraphim, the cherubim energy positive and the sanobim energy negative, near the morontia level (38:7.2, 38:7.3, 38:7.6).

rejected.reason: the family seraphim→serafines, cherubim→querubines needs the same Spanish plural
the reader must not bring the image of winged infants; these are working assistants

forcedChoices: masculine gender for querubín and sanobín: Spanish nouns need a gender; the papers write 'her' for some angels, but the noun stays masculine

chief-of-mystery-monitors.name: jefe de los Monitores de Misterio
chief-of-mystery-monitors.meaning: The being who presides over the college of Personalized Adjusters on Divinington and advises Master Spirit Number One (Paper 107).

rejected.reason: 'Misteriosos' describes them as secretive; the English uses 'Mystery' as a name element.

chief-of-urantia-cherubim.name: jefe de los querubines de Urantia
chief-of-urantia-cherubim.meaning: The chief of the cherubim on Urantia, who sat on the advisory council of the planetary receivers (114:1.4).

chief-of-urantia-seraphim.name: jefe de los serafines de Urantia
chief-of-urantia-seraphim.meaning: The supernaphim who commands the seraphic hosts on Urantia, a post that rotates (114:6.20, 113:0.1).

chiefs-of-assignment.name: jefes de asignación
chiefs-of-assignment.meaning: Primary supernaphim who assign service on Paradise, for example a supernaphim to command the seraphim of a reclaimed isolated world (27:0.2, 27:2.2).

rejected.reason: "destino" is reserved for destiny (guardianes del destino).

china.name: China
china.meaning: The land of eastern Asia where the yellow race built a stable civilization (79:5-8).

chinese.name: chinos
chinese.meaning: The people of China, mainly of the yellow race, with a long and stable civilization (79:8.1).

chorazin.name: Corazín
chorazin.meaning: A town of Galilee where Jesus and later his evangelists met the most general rejection of the gospel (146:4.6, 155:2.2).

christ.name: Cristo
christ.meaning: 'The anointed one'; the title given to Jesus and used for Michael after his bestowal, as in Christ Michael (128:7.10, 196:2.1).

christian-church-early.name: iglesia cristiana primitiva
aliases: naciente culto del cristianismo de Pablo
christian-church-early.meaning: The church that grew after Pentecost under Peter and Paul and that became a religion about Jesus, mixed with Greek and pagan elements (194:4.0, 195:0.1, 196:2.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes adjectives of religion in lowercase; the English capital on 'Christian' is a rule of English, not a coined term.
'Temprana' is a calque of 'early'; 'primitiva' is the plain Spanish word for the first period.

christianity.name: cristianismo
christianity.meaning: The religion about Jesus that grew after him, with more of his gospel than any other faith but with additions he did not teach (195:0.1, 196:2.1).

churches.name: iglesias
churches.meaning: Religious institutions; the papers set the visible church, a social organization, against the true church, the invisible spiritual brotherhood of Jesus (195:10.11, 195:10.14).

circuits.name: circuitos
circuits.meaning: The paths of presence, energy, and communication that bind creation, such as the personality circuit of the Father and the mind circuit of the Conjoint Actor (0:6.1).

claudia-procula.name: Claudia Prócula
claudia-procula.meaning: The wife of Pontius Pilate, who heard of Jesus through her maid and after Pilate's death became known for spreading the gospel (185:1.7).

co-ordinate-creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores Coordinados
co-ordinate-creator-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons considered as a corps of equal rank among themselves, through whom the Eternal Son functions in the local universes (6:2.2, 7:2.4, 7:5.10).

rejected.reason: Closer to 'of equal rank', but it breaks the rule that 'co-ordinate' is 'coordinar' and its family.
The chosen form can read as 'coordinated by someone'; the English means 'of the same order or rank'. A reviewer must decide.

co-ordinate-trinity-origin-beings.name: Seres Coordinados Originados en la Trinidad
co-ordinate-trinity-origin-beings.meaning: A Paradise group of Trinity-origin beings that includes the Trinity Teacher Sons, three groups of superuniverse administrators, and the Inspired Trinity Spirits (19:0.1).

rejected.form: Seres Coordinadores Originados en la Trinidad
rejected.reason: Says they co-ordinate others; the English adjective means of co-ordinate (equal) rank.
Loses 'origin'.

forcedChoices: 'Coordinados' from the done term 'co-ordinate: coordinar': The English adjective 'co-ordinate' means of equal rank or order, but Spanish 'coordinado' commonly reads as 'organized' or 'co-ordinated'; a human must check this.

conductors-of-worship.name: conductores de la adoración
conductors-of-worship.meaning: Primary supernaphim on Paradise who lead the outbursts of worship and teach ascenders how to worship so that they reach full satisfaction in less time (27:7.3, 27:7.4).

rejected.reason: "director" already renders "director" (directors of conduct).
"guías" already renders "guides" (Graduate Guides, Trinity guides).

conductors-of-worship.note: Spanish "conductor" most often means a driver. Here it must read as one who leads.

confucianism.name: confucianismo
confucianism.meaning: The moral teaching that grew from Confucius, which held that earthly order should mirror the order of heaven and placed the God concept below the Way of Heaven (94:6.10, 131:9.1).

confucius.name: Confucio
confucius.meaning: The sixth-century B.C. Chinese teacher who compiled the sayings of ancient sages and put morality in place of magic (92:5.12, 94:6.9).

conjoint-creator.name: Creador Conjunto
conjoint-creator.meaning: A title of the Infinite Spirit, the Third Person, who creates jointly with the Father and the Son and is the source of mind and manipulator of energy (9:3.5, 9:5.4, 9:5.5).

rejected.reason: Loses the 'conjoint' root that the papers also use in 'Conjoint Actor'.

constellations.name: constelaciones
constellations.meaning: The administrative divisions of a local universe, each of one hundred local systems, ruled by the Most Highs (43:0.2, Paper 43).

rejected.reason: The ordinary sense of 'constelación' is a visible star pattern; the reader must not bring that sense. The same is true of the English, so the plain word stays.

consuls-universe.name: cónsules (del universo)
consuls-universe.meaning: Representatives of constellations to one another and to the universe headquarters, appointed by legislative decree, often Vorondadek Sons (33:6.4, 35:5.5).

consummator-of-universe-destiny.name: Consumador del Destino del Universo
consummator-of-universe-destiny.meaning: An unrevealed agent who probably consummates destiny, an act probably involved with the Supreme and the Ultimate in the Trinity Absolute (106:7.3).

rejected.reason: Not current Spanish; "universal" is kept for "universal".
The reader must take it as "one who brings to completion", not "consumidor" (consumer).

contact-personalities.name: personalidades de contacto
contact-personalities.meaning: The few (fewer than a score) reservists who are conscious of their role as points of contact between superhuman beings and mortals, and the midwayers who serve these contacts (114:7.8, 77:8.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an office 'contact person'; and 'person' is a different English word.

corinth.name: Corinto
corinth.meaning: The capital of the Roman province of Achaia, visited by Jesus on his return from Rome (133:2.5).

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.name: personal corpóreo de los Príncipes Planetarios
corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.meaning: The one hundred ascendant volunteers who came with a Planetary Prince in material bodies as his visible helpers; on Urantia they were Caligastia's staff (77:1.2, 77:2.2, 66:4.10).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use "cuerpo" for "staff" (Van, del cuerpo del Príncipe), but "cuerpo corpóreo" repeats itself and "cuerpo" also means the body. "personal" avoids it.
Military sense.

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.note: Conflict with the earlier term "Van (del cuerpo del Príncipe)", where staff = "cuerpo". A human must decide which word "staff" takes everywhere.

corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados Conjuntos
corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, located on Vicegerington, into which Havona natives are also received (31:1.5, 30:2.135).

rejected.reason: Decides that 'conjoint' modifies 'trinitized'; the English leaves it open.
Coins a new word and also closes the reading.

forcedChoices: Spanish agreement makes 'Conjuntos' grammatically modify 'Finalitarios'. A reader can still take it as 'jointly trinitized'; the done term 'Creador Conjunto' supports 'Conjunto' for 'Conjoint'.

corps-of-havona-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios de Havona
corps-of-havona-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, a possible supreme destiny for Havona natives (31:1.5, 30:2.136).

corps-of-mortal-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales
corps-of-mortal-finaliters.meaning: The corps that is the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals, with other groups also assigned to it (31:0.1, 107:2.7).

rejected.reason: Kept as the alias for 'Corps of the Finality' because it pairs with 'finalitario', but Spanish 'finalidad' usually means 'purpose', not 'final state'. A human reviewer must decide; an alternative is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios del Paraíso
corps-of-paradise-finaliters.meaning: The second of the seven finaliter corps in the Uversa register (30:2.133, 31:10.3).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Kept for the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality'.
Breaks the pattern 'Paradise X' = 'X del Paraíso' in the done terms.

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.note: The English aliases for this term list 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and 'finaliter corps', but the papers use those for all seven corps (22:8.6). The papers name this corps only in two lists, so its exact membership is implied, not stated.

corps-of-permanent-citizens.name: cuerpo de ciudadanos permanentes
corps-of-permanent-citizens.meaning: The resident orders of beings who form the stable population of administrative worlds, such as the Material Sons on Jerusem and the susatia on Salvington (37:9.7, 37:9.12, 76:6.3).

corps-of-seraphic-completion.name: Cuerpo de Culminación Seráfica
corps-of-seraphic-completion.meaning: The corps of seraphim who traversed the circles of Seraphington, attained Paradise, and received the embrace of the Eternal Son (39:9.1).

rejected.reason: exists but is rare and stiff
suggests an ending or a stop, not an attainment

corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trascendentales
corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven Paradise finaliter corps, the corps related to transcendental service, to which Havona natives are also admitted (31:0, 31:8).

corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados
corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: The finality corps that appears to be the supreme destiny of most creature-trinitized sons, one of the seven Paradise Corps of the Finality (22:8.6, 26:11.2).

rejected.reason: The article is not in the English and breaks the pattern of 'Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales'.

cosmic-consciousness.name: conciencia cósmica
cosmic-consciousness.meaning: Awareness of the realities of the universe beyond the material and local outlook; the term itself is not defined in the papers.

rejected.reason: Also valid; 'conciencia' is the more common spelling across Latin America.
The reader must not bring this; the sense is awareness.

cosmic-mind.name: mente cósmica
cosmic-mind.meaning: The sevenfold mind of time and space, a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center, ministered by the Seven Master Spirits to the superuniverses (0:6.1, 16:6).

rejected.reason: Collides with 'Universal Mind' (Mente Universal).

counselors-and-advisers.name: consejeros y asesores
counselors-and-advisers.meaning: The sixth order of secondary supernaphim, who counsel Paradise pilgrims and also comfort those who fail in their first effort at Deity attainment (26:4.8, 26:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'consultor' suggests a paid business consultant.

counselors-and-advisers.note: The same English phrase is used as plain words for the Unions of Days (18:6.1); there it is not the name of an order.

courtesy-colonies.name: colonias de cortesía
courtesy-colonies.meaning: Groups of visiting beings who reside on headquarters worlds by courtesy, such as star students, celestial artisans, and reversion directors (46:5.30, 18:5.2, 37:10).

rejected.reason: Interprets the term instead of keeping the English word 'courtesy'.

creative-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre Creativos
creative-mother-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits seen in their creative partnership with the Creator Sons (Paper 34, 39:1.2 'Creative Spirit').

rejected.reason: 'Creadores' is fixed for 'Creator' (Hijos Creadores); 'Creative' is a different English word.
The reader must not bring the artistic or marketing sense; it means 'creating'.

creative-spirits.name: Espíritus Creativos
creative-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits, Creative Daughters of the Infinite Spirit, who create and administer with the Creator Sons (8:5.3, 39:1.2).

rejected.reason: Merges 'Creative' with 'Creator'; the papers keep the two words apart.

creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores
creator-sons.meaning: The makers and rulers of the local universes, Paradise Sons of the order of Michael, born of the Father and the Eternal Son (21:0.1, 32:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Michael' is here the name of an order of Sons; the Spanish name 'Miguel' brings in the archangel and a common personal name. See michael-of-nebadon.

creature-trinitized-sons.name: hijos trinitizados por criaturas
creature-trinitized-sons.meaning: Sons brought into being by the trinitizing union of two high creatures, such as finaliters and Paradise-Havona personalities, as distinct from those trinitized by Deity (22:0.5, 22:7.8).

rejected.reason: Singular suggests one creature; trinitization needs two (22:7.8).
Calque of the English hyphen; not natural Spanish.

creatures.name: criaturas
creatures.meaning: Any created being, as distinct from the Creator; finite realities 'always have beginnings — they are created', and the creature stands in relation to the Universal Creator (0:1.11, 1:4.5, 3:4.7).

rejected.reason: Too broad; loses the 'created' sense that the papers stress.
Ordinary senses the reader must not bring: a small child, a monster or beast. The papers mean only 'created being'.

cretaceous.name: Cretácico
cretaceous.meaning: The geological period of flowering plants and the decline of the great reptiles (60:3).

rejected.reason: Less common in current Spanish geology.

crete.name: Creta
crete.meaning: The island settled about 12,000 B.C. by a brilliant tribe of Andites skilled in crafts (80:7.2).

cro-magnons.name: Cromañones
cro-magnons.meaning: The vigorous European people from the blend of Andites with the blue race, the biologic foundation of the modern European races (80:3.3, 80:5.7).

rejected.reason: Spanish has the adapted form "cromañón".

cro-magnons.note: Spanish usually writes "cromañón" in lowercase; the capital follows rule 1 and the other race names (Andonitas). A human can decide.

custodians-of-knowledge.name: custodios del conocimiento
custodians-of-knowledge.meaning: Primary supernaphim who are living libraries on Paradise, in whom the facts of the universes are recorded and who classify knowledge into seven grand orders (27:5.1, 27:5.5, 26:3.5).

rejected.reason: 'guardián' is used for 'guardian' in the done terms; 'custodian' is 'custodio' (Trinitized Custodians).

custodians-of-records.name: Custodios de los Registros
custodians-of-records.meaning: Senior chief recorders among the tertiary supernaphim of Havona, chosen as permanent keepers of the formal archives of Paradise, in contrast to the living records held by the custodians of knowledge (25:5.1, 25:6.5).

rejected.reason: "guardián" already renders "guardian"; "Custodians" is "Custodios" in Trinitized Custodians.
The English says records, not archives; "archivos" is kept for "archives" in 25:5.1.

cybele.name: Cibeles
cybele.meaning: The Phrygian goddess, mother of Attis, whose cult the papers list among the mystery cults (98:4.3, 98:5.5).

cymboyton.name: Cymboyton
cymboyton.meaning: The wealthy merchant of Urmia who, with his three sons, built the temple of religion there (134:3.2).

cynicism-religion.name: cinismo (religión)
cynicism-religion.meaning: The doctrine of the Cynics, which the papers say had formerly been more a religion than a philosophy, drawn largely from remnants of Melchizedek's teachings and preached to common people (121:4.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes the names of schools and religions in lowercase, as in "budismo" in the terms already done.
Loses the noun that the English uses; the papers stress that it was more a religion than a school.

cynicism-religion.note: Ordinary Spanish "cinismo" means shamelessness or contempt for others. The reader must take it here as the ancient school only; the qualifier "(religión)" helps.

cynics.name: cínicos
cynics.meaning: Wandering preachers of faith and trust in God who kept the Salem teachings in a fairly pure form in Roman Europe and were later absorbed into early Christianity (98:0.2, 98:3.9, 121:4.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes members of a school in lowercase, as with "fariseos".
The papers call them preachers more than philosophers (98:3.9); adding "filósofos" narrows the sense.

cynics.note: Ordinary "cínico" means a shameless or scornful person. Context must show the ancient school.

dalamatia.name: Dalamatia
dalamatia.meaning: The headquarters city of the Planetary Prince Caligastia on Urantia, near the Persian Gulf, later submerged (66:3).

daligastia.name: Daligastia
daligastia.meaning: A secondary Lanonandek Son, the associate-assistant of the Planetary Prince Caligastia and head of the ten councils, who joined the rebellion (66:2.2, 67:2.1).

dan-city.name: Dan (ciudad)
dan-city.meaning: The northern town of Palestine also called Caesarea-Philippi (134:7.5, 155:2.1).

daniel.name: Daniel
daniel.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who understood that 'the Most High rules in the kingdom of men' (43:3.4).

dark-gravity-bodies.name: cuerpos oscuros de gravedad
dark-gravity-bodies.meaning: The enormous dark masses beyond the seventh Havona circuit that neither reflect nor absorb light and hide Havona from view (14:1.14, 12:1.10).

rejected.reason: Natural, but "de gravedad" keeps the word "gravedad" used in the other terms.

dark-islands-of-space.name: islas oscuras del espacio
dark-islands-of-space.meaning: Dead suns and other large masses without light and heat that hold neighboring systems in gravity balance (15:6.11, 15:5.11).

david-king.name: David (rey)
david-king.meaning: The king of Israel who made Jerusalem his capital (97:9).

david-zebedee.name: David Zebedeo
david-zebedee.meaning: David Zebedee, brother of James and John, who ran the messenger service of Jesus' ministry (163:0.1).

dawn-mammals.name: mamíferos del alba
dawn-mammals.meaning: The small, large-brained animals that walked mostly on their hind legs, which suddenly appeared from the North American lemur stock and gave rise to the mid-mammals (61:6.1, 62:4.7).

rejected.reason: A general description, not the coined name.
A real scientific term for a different group.

daynals-order-of.name: Daynales, orden de los
daynals-order-of.meaning: The Trinity Teacher Sons, Paradise Sons who are the true teachers of ascending personalities and whose missions lead a world toward light and life (20:9.4, 20:10.4).

decapolis.name: Decápolis
decapolis.meaning: The region of cities east of the Jordan where Jesus and his followers made a mission (157:2.2, 128:3.2).

deccan.name: Decán
deccan.meaning: The southern plateau of India, into which the Andites slowly moved southward about 15,000 B.C. (79:2.4).

rejected.reason: English spelling; Spanish geography uses Decán.

deity.name: Deidad
deity.meaning: Divine reality as it functions on diverse levels, personal or not, divinely co-ordinated (0:1.1, 16:0.1).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'divinity' as a separate term for the quality of Deity (Foreword section 'Deity and Divinity').

deity-absolute.name: Absoluto de la Deidad
deity-absolute.meaning: The potential that the Father's free will segregated from total infinite reality, within which all divinity activities take place; the Qualified Absolute (0:10.1, 0:11.6).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish; reads as a typing error.
That is the form of 'Absolute Deity', a different term; the two must stay distinct.

deity-trinitized-sons.name: Hijos trinitizados por la Deidad
deity-trinitized-sons.meaning: The first group of Trinitized Sons of God, unrevealed in the papers (22:0.2, 22:0.5).

rejected.reason: Calque of the English compound.
'Deity' and 'God' are distinct terms (Deidad, Dios).

deity-ultimate.name: Deidad Última
deity-ultimate.meaning: A designation of God the Ultimate, Deity on the second level of unifying divinity expression as overcontroller of the master universe (0:1.10, 0:9.1).

rejected.reason: Would mirror 'Absoluto de la Deidad', but that term names a distinct Absolute; this term only names God the Ultimate.
Both English forms name the same being, so one Spanish form is acceptable; a reviewer should confirm.

deliverer.name: Libertador
deliverer.meaning: One who delivers a people, as in the Jewish hope of a Messiah-deliverer; the papers say Jesus was not the expected deliverer of the Jews but the world's deliverer (121:2.7, 122:4.2, 136:1.1).

rejected.reason: "Savior" is a different English word; the papers keep deliverance and salvation apart (97:8.3).
Adds the idea of ransom, which the English does not carry.

descending-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios descendentes
descending-sons-of-god.meaning: Sons of God of high divine origin who serve on the worlds of time and space to help the ascending sons of God in their Paradise climb (20:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'Descendiente' means offspring or descendant, not one who goes down.

designers-and-embellishers.name: diseñadores y embellecedores
designers-and-embellishers.meaning: A group of the celestial artisans who create works of beauty for morontia and spirit beings (44:0.11).

directors-of-conduct.name: directores de la conducta
directors-of-conduct.meaning: Primary supernaphim who teach new arrivals on Paradise the proper usages of conduct there and guide them so that they avoid confusion (27:4.1, 27:4.3).

discerners-of-spirits.name: Discernidores de Espíritus
discerners-of-spirits.meaning: Secondary seconaphim attached to the Universal Censors who, by inherent spiritual insight, present unerring portraits of the soul and motives of a being (28:5.20).

rejected.reason: 'Discerniente' is an adjective (discerning), not an agent noun.
Changes the idea: they discern and present; the Censors judge.

divine-counselors.name: Consejeros Divinos
divine-counselors.meaning: An order of Trinity-origin beings who are the counsel of the Paradise Trinity to the superuniverses and sit with Perfectors of Wisdom and Universal Censors (19:0.1, 22:1.13).

rejected.reason: 'Asesor' reads as a hired technical adviser; 'consejero' carries counsel and wisdom.

divine-executioners.name: ejecutores divinos
divine-executioners.meaning: The quasi-material fourth members of a conciliating commission, who carry out the decisions of the commission (25:2.8, 25:3.5, 29:4.15).

rejected.reason: 'verdugo' is only the one who puts a person to death; the papers mean the one who executes decisions.
'ejecutante' is mainly a musical performer.

divine-executioners.note: 'ejecutor' can also suggest one who kills; the context (executing decisions) supports the sense 'one who carries out'.

divinington.name: Divinington
divinington.meaning: The first sacred world of the Father near Paradise, the 'bosom of the Father' and Paradise rendezvous of the Thought Adjusters (13:1.4).

divinity.name: divinidad
divinity.meaning: The unifying quality of Deity as creatures comprehend it: truth, beauty, and goodness; love, mercy, and ministry in personality; justice, power, and sovereignty on impersonal levels (0:1.2, 0:1.15, 0:1.17).

rejected.reason: 'Deidad' is the term for Deity; 'divinity' is its quality, so the two forms must differ.
In everyday Spanish 'una divinidad' is a god or goddess, and 'divinidad' can mean 'something lovely'. The reader must not bring either sense.

dravidians.name: drávidas
dravidians.meaning: The mixed people of India that came from Andite conquerors blending with native stock (79:3.1).

dual-origin-beings.name: seres de origen dual
dual-origin-beings.meaning: Beings who originate in any two of the Paradise Deities, or who are created by any two beings descended from them (30:1.29).

rejected.reason: Also natural, but 'dual' matches 'triune' as a parallel classification term.

eber.name: Eber
eber.meaning: The officer of the Sanhedrin sent to arrest Jesus, who refused and defended him before the rulers (162:2.6, 162:2.9).

edentia.name: Edentia
edentia.meaning: The headquarters world of the constellation Norlatiadek, seat of the Most Highs (43:0.1).

egypt.name: Egipto
egypt.meaning: Egypt, the land of the Nile valley and its ancient civilization (95:2.1).

el-elyon.name: El Elyon
el-elyon.meaning: The Most High God of heaven, the term for Melchizedek's doctrine of Deity after his time at Salem (96:1.4, 96:4.2).

elijah-mark.name: Elías Marcos
elijah-mark.meaning: The father of John Mark, at whose Jerusalem home Jesus ate the Last Supper with the apostles (183:2.1).

elijah-prophet.name: Elías (profeta)
elijah-prophet.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who denounced Ahab for the murder of Naboth and defended the old land mores against the Baalim (97:9.19).

elizabeth-mother-of-john-the-baptist.name: Isabel (madre de Juan el Bautista)
elizabeth-mother-of-john-the-baptist.meaning: The wife of Zacharias and mother of John the Baptist, a relative of Mary, who with Zacharias believed Jesus would be the Messiah (122:8.4).

rejected.reason: Used in some Bible versions; Isabel is the common Spanish name.

elohim.name: Elohim
elohim.meaning: The name under which a three-in-one God concept, a Trinity, was worshiped; Jesus never claimed to be Elohim in the flesh, only the revelation of the Father (96:1.8, 169:4.9).

endor.name: Endor
endor.meaning: A town in Galilee where Joseph worked and where Jesus rested from the crowds and told the story of King Saul and the witch of Endor (123:3.8, 146:7.1).

energy.name: energía
energy.meaning: An all-inclusive term for spiritual, mindal, and material realms; physical energy denotes all phases and forms of phenomenal motion, action, and potential (0:6.2, 0:6.3).

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) energy as only a physical quantity
rejected.reason: The reader must not limit it to physics; 0:6.2 applies it to spirit and mind.

energy-manipulators.name: manipuladores de energía
energy-manipulators.meaning: The celestial artisans, and also living physical controllers, who study and handle physical, mind, and spiritual energies (44:5.4, 41:2.4).

rejected.reason: The done list uses 'manipuladores de energía mental' and 'manipuladores de energía espiritual'.

energy-transformers.name: transformadores de energía
energy-transformers.meaning: Among the more personal orders of the Master Physical Controllers, created by the Supreme Power Directors and Center Supervisors; they command on inhabited worlds when no associate power director is present (29:4.23).

rejected.reason: Reads as an adjective of a device.

energy-transformers.note: A reader can take 'transformadores' as electrical devices; the context shows they are living beings.

energy-transmitters.name: transmisores de energía
energy-transmitters.meaning: Living beings of the Master Physical Controllers who relay energy and can receive and transmit intelligence but cannot start a communication (67:6.9, 39:5.14).

engedi.name: Engadi
engedi.meaning: A place by the Dead Sea where the Nazarite colony under Abner lived, often visited by John the Baptist (135:2.3, 135:2.4).

rejected.reason: Spanish has its own established form for this biblical place.

english-language.name: lengua inglesa
english-language.meaning: The language into which the revelators were authorized to translate the papers, and whose limits they note (0:0.1, 42:2.1).

enoch.name: Enoc
enoch.meaning: The son of Cain and Remona who became head of the Elamite Nodites, the first Urantia mortal to fuse with his Thought Adjuster during life in the flesh, now one of the four and twenty counselors (76:2.9, 45:4.13); the so-called Book of Enoch bears his name (126:3.8).

ensa.name: Ensa
ensa.meaning: The minor sector of one hundred local universes, with capital Uminor the third, in which Nebadon lies (15:14.7, 18:5.5).

ephesus.name: Éfeso
ephesus.meaning: The capital of the Roman province of Asia, with the temple of Artemis; Jesus visited it with Gonod and Ganid, and John Zebedee later settled and died there (133:6.1, 139:4.15).

ephraim.name: Efraín
ephraim.meaning: The hill country where Israelite consciousness began, and a name for the northern kingdom of Israel (97:9.2, 97:9.11, 97:9.21).

epochal-revelations.name: revelaciones epocales
epochal-revelations.meaning: Revelation of truth presented to a world by a celestial agency, group, or personality, in contrast to autorevelation by the indwelling Adjuster (101:4.3, 92:3.5).

rejected.reason: Can read as "revelations typical of a period" (period style).
"trascendental" is reserved for transcendental.

epochal-revelations.note: Family "revelation": root "revelación" (autorrevelación for autorevelation). "epocal" is in the dictionary but uncommon; it reads as a term, as the English does.

error.name: error
error.meaning: An intellectual mistake, a misconception that suggests lack of intellectual keenness, with no moral guilt in itself (67:1.4, 67:1.5).

rejected.reason: Too casual for the defined term.

eskimos.name: esquimales
eskimos.meaning: Descendants of the Urantia aborigines who crossed from Greenland into North America some eighty thousand years ago (64:7.18).

eternal-son.name: Hijo Eterno
eternal-son.meaning: The Second Source and Center, the perfect expression of the Father's first absolute thought, the Word-God (6:0.1, 8:0.1).

eternals-of-days.name: Eternos de Días
eternals-of-days.meaning: The Supreme Trinity Personalities who each rule one Havona world, divine equals of the Ancients of Days (18:2.2, 18:4.6).

rejected.reason: Follows "Ancianos de Días" and "Uniones de Días" in the terms already done.

eternity.name: eternidad
eternity.meaning: Timeless existence, the everlasting now, in which potential infinity is inseparable (0:11.12, 13:1.9).

rejected.reason: Means endless duration in time, which is the opposite of timelessness.

ethics.name: ética
ethics.meaning: The principles of right relations between persons, growing from the facts of origin; ethics is progressive, unlike static traditional morality.

rejected.reason: The papers distinguish ethics from morality.

euphrates-river.name: río Éufrates
euphrates-river.meaning: One of the two rivers of Mesopotamia.

europe.name: Europa
europe.meaning: The continent of Europe, settled by the blue man and later by the Andites (80:4.5, 80:5.8).

evangelists.name: evangelistas
evangelists.meaning: The preachers of the gospel trained by the apostles under Jesus, some later ordained as the seventy messengers of the kingdom (148:1.4, 149:0.2).

rejected.reason: Loses the link with "evangelio" (gospel).

evangelists.note: Same Spanish word as in "evangelistas seráficos" (seraphic evangels) in the terms already done. The adjective "seráficos" separates them, but a human must check the overlap.

eve.name: Eva
eve.meaning: The Material Daughter who came with Adam to Urantia to uplift the races (40:2.2).

eventuated-transcendental-beings.name: seres trascendentales eventuados
eventuated-transcendental-beings.meaning: Transcendental beings who neither create nor are created but are eventuated, functioning on absonite levels (0:1.12, 31:8).

rejected.reason: "eventual" means "possible" or "temporary".

eventuation.name: eventuación
eventuation.meaning: The coming into being of absonite realities and beings, neither creation nor evolution; they "simply are" (0:1.12, 0:9.1, 0:9.2).

rejected.reason: The Spanish adjective "eventual" means "possible" or "temporary"; the reader must not carry it into "eventuar".
Has the Christian sense of the coming of Christ.
Means an event, not a mode of coming into being.

evil.name: mal
evil.meaning: The partial or unknowing transgression of divine law, the misadaptation of immaturity, which becomes sin only when chosen knowingly (67:1.4, 67:1.5, 132:2.1).

rejected.reason: Means wickedness of character, which is closer to sin; kept only as an alias.
The reader must not bring the sense of a personal or cosmic power of evil, nor illness ("un mal").

experientials.name: experienciales
experientials.meaning: Realities that come to be through experience and growth, as the Supreme and the Ultimate are; the opposite of existential (0:1.14, 0:4.9, 0:7.5).

rejected.reason: Means "by experiment" or "trial"; a false friend.
Psychological and regional; the English is a coined term.

ezekiel.name: Ezequiel
ezekiel.meaning: A Hebrew prophet who taught personal responsibility, proclaimed deliverance through the service of devotion, and foretold a new spirit within man (97:8.3, 145:2.7).

faith.name: fe
faith.meaning: The living, personal trust by which a person grasps the truth of sonship with God; the assurance of sonship is the experience of faith (140:10.9, 193:0.4, 196:3.34).

rejected.reason: The papers set belief apart from faith; 'creencia' is the word for belief.
Is trust in general and collides with 'espíritus de la confianza'.

faithful-of-days-of-edentia.name: Fiel de Días de Edentia
faithful-of-days-of-edentia.meaning: The Trinity Son of Paradise on Edentia who represents Immanuel and counsels the Most Highs of the constellation only when asked (43:4.2, 18:7.3).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use "de Días" without the article (Ancianos de Días, Uniones de Días).

faithfuls-of-days.name: Fieles de Días
faithfuls-of-days.meaning: Trinity-origin personalities, seventy million in number, who are the Paradise advisers to the rulers of the constellations (18:7.1).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of 'Ancianos de Días' and 'Uniones de Días'.

father-absolute.name: Padre-Absoluto
father-absolute.meaning: The Universal Father as the creator of the central universe and Father of all Creators, absolute in liberty of action (4:4.4, 10:3.8, 4:4.9).

rejected.reason: Without the hyphen it reads as a description ('the absolute father'); the English hyphen marks a name, like 'Father-Infinite'.

father-fused-mortals.name: mortales fusionados con el Padre
father-fused-mortals.meaning: Mortals who fuse with their Thought Adjuster, a fragment of the Universal Father; the same as Adjuster-fused mortals (40:9.1, 22:6.1).

father-melchizedek.name: Padre Melquisedec
father-melchizedek.meaning: The first Melchizedek of Nebadon, who with the Creator Son and Creative Spirit brought the order into being and acts for Gabriel in his absence (93:1.2).

father-s-house.name: casa del Padre
father-s-house.meaning: Paradise as the eternal residence of the Father (11:3.3), and in Jesus' words the home to which the lost return (159:5.16) and which holds many mansions (30:4.17).

father-s-way.name: Camino del Padre
father-s-way.meaning: The moral law of seven commands that Hap gave the early races in Dalamatia (66:7.8).

rejected.reason: Keeps only the sense 'manner'; 'camino' carries both 'path' and 'way of life'.
Adds a word the English does not use.

forcedChoices: English 'way' is both 'path' and 'manner'; 'camino' keeps both readings better than another word.

fatherhood-of-god.name: paternidad de Dios
fatherhood-of-god.meaning: The truth that God is the Father of all persons, which the gospel of the kingdom proclaims with the sonship of man (193:0.4).

rejected.reason: Means sponsorship or godfathership, a different relationship.

finaliter-corps.name: cuerpo de finalitarios
finaliter-corps.meaning: Any of the corps into which beings who attain Paradise are mustered; the papers speak of seven such corps (19:6.3, 30:4.31, 31:10.20).

rejected.reason: Grammatical, but 'finalitario' as an adjective is less clear than the noun phrase.
Reads as 'the last body'.

finaliter-corps.note: The English uses both 'finaliter corps' and 'finality corps' (30:4.31). 'cuerpo de la finalidad' is listed as an alias for the second English form.

finaliters.name: finalitarios
finaliters.meaning: Ascenders who complete the Paradise ascension and enter the Corps of the Finality, the present known destination of Adjuster-fused mortals (31:0.1, 107:2.7).

rejected.reason: Means a finalist in a contest.
Means those who finish or end a thing.

finaliters-world.name: mundo de los finalitarios
finaliters-world.meaning: The system world on which finaliters are received and where half the planet holds the probation nursery for children of surviving mortals (45:6.7, 45:6.8, 47:1.4).

rejected.reason: The English names the world after the finaliters, not after the abstract finality.
Reads as 'the last world'; loses the link to the finaliters.

first-cause.name: Primera Causa
first-cause.meaning: God as science reaches him by reason: the origin of all causes; revelation shows that this First Cause and the God of salvation are one Deity (4:4.7, 101:2.3, 101:2.7, 118:4.1).

rejected.reason: Also correct, but the plain word order matches the English and reads naturally in all regions.

first-experiential-trinity.name: primera Trinidad experiencial
first-experiential-trinity.meaning: The union of the Supreme Creators, the Supreme Being, and the Architects of the Master Universe, also called the Trinity Ultimate (106:3.2, 31:9.14, 0:12.3).

rejected.reason: 'Experimental' means 'trial' or 'test'.

force.name: fuerza
force.meaning: A broad term like energy, for spiritual, mindal, and material realms; in physics, cosmic force means energies from the Unqualified Absolute not yet responsive to Paradise gravity (0:6.2, 0:6.5).

foundation-of-spiritual-progress.name: Fundación del Progreso Espiritual
foundation-of-spiritual-progress.meaning: An institution on a neighboring planet that supervises spiritual teachers who visit families, supported by voluntary gifts (Paper 72).

rejected.reason: Adds a purpose that the English 'of' does not state.

four-and-twenty-counselors.name: veinticuatro consejeros
four-and-twenty-counselors.meaning: A commission of twenty-four ascended Urantians on Jerusem, Michael's personal agents and advisory-control body for Urantia (45:4, 76:6.3).

rejected.reason: Spanish has no archaic 'four and twenty' order; it reads as an error.

forcedChoices: plain 'veinticuatro': Spanish cannot keep the archaic English numeral order.

fourth-creatures-cherubim.name: cuartas criaturas (querubines)
fourth-creatures-cherubim.meaning: Every fourth cherubim and sanobim, quasi-material and near the morontia level, useful in borderland work (38:7.6, 38:7.7).

rejected.reason: reads as an odd adjective; the ordinal precedes in Spanish

fourth-creatures-havona-servitals.name: cuartas criaturas (Servitales de Havona)
aliases: cuartas criaturas de los Servitales de Havona
fourth-creatures-havona-servitals.meaning: Every fourth Havona Servital, a semiphysical being nearer to the physical power directors, able to discern both spirit and material beings (25:1.3, 44:0.17).

rejected.reason: Unnatural word order in Spanish.

fourth-creatures-universal-conciliators.name: cuartas criaturas (Conciliadores Universales)
fourth-creatures-universal-conciliators.meaning: The quasi-material member of each conciliating commission, the Divine Executioner, almost visible to mortals (25:2.5, 25:2.8).

frandalanks.name: frandalanks
frandalanks.meaning: The most numerous Master Physical Controllers, created in thirty divisions, which act as living gauges of presence, pressure, and velocity of force-energy (29:4.36, 29:4.37).

rejected.reason: Adapting a name that exists only in this book breaks rule 3.

free-will.name: libre albedrío
free-will.meaning: The capacity of a personal creature to choose within its limits, the mark of will creatures that makes moral decision and survival possible (5:6, 112:5, 118:6).

rejected.reason: Shows the family root "voluntad" but is less natural as the name of the faculty; kept as the alias "voluntad libre" where the text stresses the will.

fusion.name: fusión
fusion.meaning: The eternal union of the surviving soul with a divine spirit fragment, of the Father (Adjuster), the Son, or the Spirit; a creature is fused with only one (40:9.1, 40:10.10).

rejected.reason: Too general; loses the coined term.
The reader must not bring the physical sense of 'fusión' to this term.

gabriel.name: Gabriel
gabriel.meaning: The Bright and Morning Star, first creation of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit and chief executive of Nebadon (33:4.1).

rejected.reason: 'Lucero' is the planet Venus and is a traditional name for Lucifer; that sense is the opposite of what the authors mean.

gadara.name: Gadara
gadara.meaning: A town of the Decapolis where Thomas Didymus once worked as a carpenter and stone mason, and where the apostles did personal work (138:2.5, 138:9.3).

galaxies.name: galaxias
galaxies.meaning: Vast star systems; in outer space they swing around Paradise in orderly procession, separated by quiet zones, and 375 million new ones will be seen by future telescopes (11:7.7, 12:2.3).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'nebulae' as a separate word; a galaxy is not a nebula.

galilee.name: Galilea
galilee.meaning: The northern province of Palestine where Jesus did much of his ministry; Sepphoris and later Tiberias were its capitals (129:1.2).

ganges.name: Ganges
ganges.meaning: The great river of India whose delta formed largely in the last fifty thousand years (59:6.9, 79:2.1).

ganid.name: Ganid
ganid.meaning: The young Indian son of Gonod whom Jesus tutored on their journey through the Mediterranean world (130:0.3, 133:1.1, 133:3.5).

garden-of-eden.name: Jardín del Edén
garden-of-eden.meaning: The headquarters of Adam and Eve on a Mediterranean peninsula, later submerged.

rejected.reason: Collides with the done term 'Paraíso'.

gautama-siddhartha.name: Gautama Siddhartha
gautama-siddhartha.meaning: The Indian teacher whose teachings contained far more truth than survives in the modern cults that bear his name (94:7.8).

rejected.reason: Changes the order and the spelling of the English form.

gentiles.name: gentiles
gentiles.meaning: The non-Jewish peoples of the time of Jesus, morally somewhat below the Jews but with natural goodness in which the gospel could grow (121:4.1, 128:2.5).

rejected.reason: Adds a religious judgment; the English means only non-Jewish.

gerasa.name: Gerasa
gerasa.meaning: A city of the Decapolis on Jesus' routes between Galilee and Jerusalem (128:3.2, 152:7.1).

germany.name: Alemania
germany.meaning: The present European country, named in the papers for its geological deposits and racial history (59:4.8, 60:1.4).

gethsemane.name: Getsemaní
gethsemane.meaning: A park near Jerusalem beyond the brook Kidron, beside which Jesus and the apostles camped and where he was arrested (182:0.1).

gilboa.name: Gilboa
gilboa.meaning: The mountain in northern Palestine where the Philistines defeated Saul; the pilgrims from Nazareth passed its base on the road to Jerusalem (97:9.13, 124:6.4).

rejected.reason: Older Spanish spelling; less common today than Gilboa.

god.name: Dios
god.meaning: God, the Universal Father, First Source and Center and the eternal God who dwells on Paradise (0:0.5, 1:0.1).

god-the-absolute.name: Dios el Absoluto
god-the-absolute.meaning: The experiential Deity whose actualization would follow the unification of the Absolute Trinity: the realization of absolute divinity (0:10.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as a description ('the absolute God') and breaks the pattern 'Dios el Espíritu', 'Dios el Supremo'.

god-the-sevenfold.name: Dios el Séptuple
god-the-sevenfold.meaning: The seven-level association of Deity, from the Creator Sons up to the Universal Father, that makes up for the limits of creatures and integrates the perfecting with the perfect (105:6.5, 0:9.1).

rejected.reason: Breaks the pattern of the done terms 'Dios el Absoluto' and 'Dios el Espíritu'.
'Septenario' means a seven-day period or a set of seven.

god-the-spirit.name: Dios el Espíritu
god-the-spirit.meaning: The Infinite Spirit, Third Person of the Paradise Trinity (8:0.4, 13:1.10).

rejected.reason: Drops the article and reads as a description ('God, who is spirit') instead of the name.

god-the-supreme.name: Dios el Supremo
god-the-supreme.meaning: The personal spirit reflection of the triune Paradise Deity in Havona, the first experiential Deity, unifying with the Almighty Supreme as the Supreme Being (0:7.1, 0:7.7).

god-the-ultimate.name: Dios el Último
god-the-ultimate.meaning: Personal Deity that functions on the absonite level of supertime and transcended space, eventuating from the divinity potentials of the master universe; the second experiential Deity after God the Supreme (0:9.1, 0:9.2, 0:9.5).

rejected.reason: Implies only an end point in time, against 0:9.5 (he has no end).
Without the article it reads as 'the last God'; the pattern 'Dios el X' follows Dios el Supremo and Dios el Absoluto.

forcedChoices: masculine 'el Último': The English refers to God the Ultimate with 'he' as with God the Supreme (0:7.1, 117:7.4).

gods-and-goddesses.name: dioses y diosas
gods-and-goddesses.meaning: The many deities of human religions, such as the Greek family of gods and goddesses that grew from Hellenic invaders' concepts (98:1.2).

goodness.name: bondad
goodness.meaning: With truth and beauty one of the three divine values through which creatures grasp divinity; the moral and spiritual quality of God that creatures seek and recognize (2:7, 56:10).

rejected.reason: Only kindness toward others; narrower than goodness.
The reader must not reduce it to "niceness" or mild kindness.

gospel.name: evangelio
gospel.meaning: The good news Jesus proclaimed: the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man, the kingdom received by faith (194:3.8, 170:0.1).

rejected.reason: A correct gloss, but not a single term; 'evangelio' is the plain word.
Capital reads as a book of the New Testament; the English uses lowercase for the message.

graduate-guides.name: Guías de Graduados
graduate-guides.meaning: Higher Personalities of the Infinite Spirit who conduct the training school of Havona and guide each ascending pilgrim through the circuits; some are translated Havona Servitals (24:6.4, 25:1.7).

rejected.reason: Reads as guides who themselves graduated; the English 'Graduate Guides' can mean guides of graduates (the pilgrims who graduate from the superuniverses).
Too academic and modern.

forcedChoices: 'de Graduados': English leaves open whether 'graduate' describes the guides or the pilgrims; Spanish must choose. The pilgrims arrive as graduates of the superuniverse schools (25:1.7). A reviewer must check.

grand-universe.name: gran universo
grand-universe.meaning: The seven evolving superuniverses together with the central universe of Havona, the now organized and inhabited creation (0:0.6).

rejected.reason: After the noun, "grande" is only a size description, not a name.

grandfanda.name: Grandfanda
