grandfanda.meaning: The first mortal pilgrim of time to reach Havona, from planet 341 of system 84 in constellation 62 of local universe 1,131 in superuniverse one (24:6.8, 7:5.8).

gravity.name: gravedad
gravity.meaning: The sole control of energy-matter, and by extension the drawing circuits of personality, spirit, mind, and material gravity (0:6.11).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring this; the sense is a drawing force.

gravity-messengers.name: Mensajeros de la Gravedad
gravity-messengers.meaning: Personal messengers able to transcend time and space, under the jurisdiction of Grandfanda and assigned to the primary Corps of the Finality (31:2.1, 23:3.2).

great-spirit.name: Gran Espíritu
great-spirit.meaning: The deity concept of the American red men, revived by Onamonalonton and kept from the Dalamatian teachings (64:6.7, 92:4.5).

rejected.reason: After the noun 'grande' means physical size; 'Gran' before the noun gives the sense of greatness.

greece.name: Grecia
greece.meaning: Ancient Greece and its culture and philosophy (98:1.1, 195:1.1).

greeks.name: griegos
greeks.meaning: The ancient Greek people, teachers, artists, traders, and colonizers of the Mediterranean (80:7, 98:1-2).

green-race.name: raza verde
green-race.meaning: One of the six Sangik races, among the less able primitive groups, weakened by migrations in many directions (64:6.17).

guardian-angels.name: ángeles guardianes
guardian-angels.meaning: Seraphim assigned to individual mortals or groups of mortals, who minister to them in life and keep the identity of the surviving soul until the resurrection (Paper 113).

rejected.reason: A natural devotional set phrase, but it brings a popular image of a child's protector; 'guardianes' also matches 'serafines guardianes'.
Liturgical tone and less common across Latin America.

guardians-of-destiny.name: guardianes del destino
guardians-of-destiny.meaning: Personal seraphim assigned to a mortal who reaches the third circle or makes the supreme decision, who keep the soul's survival values after death and can go with the mortal to Paradise (113:6.1, 113:7.5).

rejected.reason: Popular religious term with a different idea.

hap.name: Hap
hap.meaning: The member of Caligastia's corporeal staff who led the college of revealed religion, stayed loyal with Van, and gave the early races the moral code called 'The Father's Way' (66:7.8, 67:4.1).

havona.name: Havona
havona.meaning: The eternal central universe of perfect worlds that surrounds Paradise (0:0.5, 14:0.1).

havona-natives.name: nativos de Havona
aliases: habitantes de los mundos de Havona
havona-natives.meaning: The beings created by the Trinity who are the native inhabitants of the billion worlds of the central universe (14:4, 37:9.12).

rejected.reason: Brings an ethnic and social sense.

havona-pilgrims.name: peregrinos de Havona
havona-pilgrims.meaning: Ascending mortals who reach the central universe and pass inward through the seven circuits of Havona toward Paradise (Paper 26, 24:6.4).

rejected.reason: 'romero' is a pilgrim to a local shrine and a herb; folk sense.

havona-servitals.name: Servitales de Havona
havona-servitals.meaning: Beings created by the Master Spirits with the Supreme Power Directors, who serve in Havona and the superuniverses, and some of whom become Graduate Guides (25:1.3, 25:1.7).

rejected.reason: Too generic; the coined '-al' form reads as a term.

hebrew-language.name: lengua hebrea
hebrew-language.meaning: The language of the Hebrews, who had no general written form until they learned an alphabet from the Philistines (74:8.9).

herod-antipas.name: Herodes Antipas
herod-antipas.meaning: Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, who killed John the Baptist (135:12.1).

herod-the-great.name: Herodes el Grande
herod-the-great.meaning: The former king, father of Herod Antipas, whose Maccabean palace in Jerusalem Antipas used (185:4.1).

high-commissioners.name: Altos Comisionados
high-commissioners.meaning: Spirit-fused ascendant mortals who begin as race commissioners on the planets and rise to serve the local universe (37:5.6).
high-commissioners.note: 29:4.2 uses "high commissioners of power" in lowercase for another group (Council of Equilibrium). Translators must not confuse the two.

high-son-assistants.name: Asistentes de los Altos Hijos
high-son-assistants.meaning: Twice-trinitized sons, each the embodiment of one concept, who serve as personal aids and private secretaries to the high sons of the governments of the Ancients of Days (22:10.1, 22:1.12, 22:10.4).

rejected.reason: Reads as if the assistants are themselves high sons; they assist the high sons.
"ayudantes" is reserved for adjutant (espíritus ayudantes de la mente).

high-son-assistants.note: The English is ambiguous in form ("High Son Assistants"); 22:10.1 shows they serve the high sons, so the Spanish says "de los Altos Hijos".

high-spirit-personalities-of-circuit-con.name: altas personalidades espirituales del control de circuitos (no reveladas)
high-spirit-personalities-of-circuit-con.meaning: Unrevealed high spirit personalities who help the circuit supervisors direct the circuits for spirit messages and the transit of personalities (Paper 24).

rejected.form: altas personalidades de espíritu del control de circuitos
rejected.reason: Awkward; 'de espíritu' reads as 'spirited'.
'Superiores' is reserved for 'higher' (Personalidades Superiores del Espíritu Infinito).

higher-personalities-of-the-infinite-spi.name: Personalidades Superiores del Espíritu Infinito
higher-personalities-of-the-infinite-spi.meaning: The seven orders of higher personalities of the Infinite Spirit (Solitary Messengers, Universe Circuit Supervisors, Census Directors, Personal Aids, Associate Inspectors, Assigned Sentinels, Graduate Guides) (Paper 24, 45:1.8).

rejected.reason: 'Alta' is used for 'high' elsewhere in the papers; 'Higher' is a comparative and needs 'Superiores'.

hinduism.name: hinduismo
hinduism.meaning: The oldest and most adaptable of the major religions, an integral part of the social life of India (94:4).

holy-spirit.name: Espíritu Santo
holy-spirit.meaning: The spiritual circuit of the local universe Creative Spirit (Divine Minister), confined to the local universe, distinct from the omnipresent Infinite Spirit (8:5.3, 34:5.5, 194:2.17).

rejected.reason: Not natural Spanish for this name; 'Espíritu Santo' is the plain form and matches the scriptural phrase the papers quote.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) third person of the Christian Trinity
rejected.reason: The reader must not identify it with the Infinite Spirit; the papers define it as the circuit of the local universe Mother Spirit (8:5.3).

i-am.name: YO SOY
i-am.meaning: The philosophic concept of the Universal Father as the infinite, eternal, and absolute primal cause before any differentiation of reality (105:1.1, 105:2.1).

rejected.reason: the English keeps full capitals; keep them

iceland.name: Islandia
iceland.meaning: The northern island that in one epoch, with Greenland, connected North America and Europe (61:1.12).

idealism.name: idealismo
idealism.meaning: Devotion to high spiritual concepts and values above material ends, which in the papers must also be practical.
forcedChoices: 'idealismo': The reader must not bring the philosophical school (mind over matter) where the papers mean devotion to ideals.

identity.name: identidad
identity.meaning: The continuing sameness of a self or of an energy system, which personality can unify; in man it is at first material and temporary, and its seat can pass to the morontia soul (112:0.7, 112:5.4, 112:2.20, 112:3.7).

rejected.form: identidad (sense of a document or social group)
rejected.reason: Ordinary senses the reader must not bring: a national or social identity, or an ID card. Here it is the continuing sameness of the self.

ikhnaton.name: Akenatón
ikhnaton.meaning: The young Egyptian king who kept alive the doctrine of El Elyon, the One God, in Egypt (95:5.2).

rejected.reason: An older English spelling; rule 2 asks for the standard Spanish form of a historical person.

ikhnaton.note: Spanish spellings vary (Akenatón, Ajenatón, Akhenatón). A human can choose one for the whole book.

immanuel.name: Immanuel
immanuel.meaning: The Union of Days assigned to Nebadon, ambassador of the Paradise Trinity to Michael, whose name means 'God with us' (33:4).

rejected.reason: The usual Spanish form of the biblical name; but here it names a particular being of this book, so the English spelling stays to keep the person distinct from the prophecy.

impersonal.name: impersonal
impersonal.meaning: Without personality; the impersonal never transmutes directly into the personal (0:5.4, 0:1.17, 56:9.5).

rejected.reason: 'Nonpersonal' is a separate English word in the papers (0:5.2, 0:5.5).
The reader must not read it as a lack of warmth.

imports-of-time.name: Alcances del Tiempo
imports-of-time.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who evaluate time: they show how much time an undertaking requires, are consulted to forecast events, and testify that every being had time to choose (28:6.10, 28:6.11).

rejected.reason: "significados" already renders "meanings", and "Significances of Origins" is a sister order.
Unnatural plural, and it reads as "how important time is".
"importe" means an amount of money.
"time evaluators" is the papers' description (28:6.11), not the name.

imports-of-time.note: English "import" here means the bearing or significance of time. No Spanish noun matches it well. A human must choose.

india.name: India
india.meaning: The land of India, home of a very mixed population of all the races (79:2.1).

rejected.reason: Refers to the religion; 'indio' is the gentilic. Note that 'indio' can also mean a native American in Latin America; context decides.

indigo-race.name: raza índigo
indigo-race.meaning: The sixth of the Sangik colored races, which migrated to Africa and stayed there (64:6).

rejected.reason: 'añil' is correct but less known for the color in all countries; 'índigo' matches the English.

infinite.name: Infinito
infinite.meaning: The fullness, the finality, implied by the primacy of the First Source and Center; an actual value-level of the free will of the Universal Father, also called the Father-Infinite (0:3.24, 0:3.25).

rejected.reason: Done as the word for 'infinity'; the Foreword keeps 'the Infinite' and 'infinity' apart (0:3.24).
Adds 'being', which the English does not say.

infinite.note: Same letters as the done adjective 'infinite: infinito'; only the capital and the article 'el' mark the noun. The reader must not take it as the plain adjective.

infinite-mind.name: Mente Infinita
infinite-mind.meaning: The mind of the Infinite Spirit, present throughout creation through the intelligence circuits.

infinite-spirit.name: Espíritu Infinito
infinite-spirit.meaning: The Third Person of Deity, the agent of the combined action of the Father and the Son, the God of Action and source of mind (8:0.1, 8:1.1, 23:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Agente' can read as a representative or a police agent; 'Actor' keeps the sense of the one who acts, as in the English.
'Manipulador' carries a sense of deceit in Spanish, as 'manipulator' does in English; kept because the English uses this word for the handling of energies. Reviewer can check.

infinity.name: infinitud
infinity.meaning: The quality and level of the infinite: the unqualified reality of the I AM, potential infinity being absolute and inseparable from eternity (0:3.21, 0:11.1, 0:11.12).

rejected.reason: Common Spanish for 'a huge number' (una infinidad de cosas); it loses the quality sense.
Reserved for 'the Infinite' (0:3.24), a different English term.

iniquity.name: iniquidad
iniquity.meaning: The willful, determined, and persistent transgression of divine law, indicative of vanishing personality control (67:1.4, 67:1.5).

rejected.reason: Too general; does not carry the persistent, willful sense.
Only injustice.

inquiring-greeks.name: griegos inquisitivos
inquiring-greeks.meaning: The Greeks who came to Philip in Jerusalem asking to see Jesus and were brought to him by Philip and Andrew (139:5.9).

rejected.reason: Calls up the Inquisition.
Suggests an investigation, not a request.

inquiring-greeks.note: 'inquiring' here means 'asking' (they asked to see Jesus). 'inquisitivos' can read as 'nosy'; a reviewer can prefer 'griegos que preguntaban'.

inspired-trinity-spirits.name: Espíritus Inspirados de la Trinidad
aliases: Espíritus Inspirados de la Trinidad del Paraíso
inspired-trinity-spirits.meaning: A somewhat impersonal, largely secret order of Trinity-origin beings whose ministry is superconscious (19:0.1).

rejected.reason: Word order can read as 'Spirits of the inspired Trinity'.
Closes a reading the English leaves open: the English does not say the Trinity inspires them.

intelligence-co-ordinators-seraphic-corp.name: coordinadores de información (Cuerpo Seráfico de Culminación)
intelligence-co-ordinators-seraphic-corp.meaning: Glorified completion seraphim who coordinate the exchange of news and information with the broadcasters (26:3.8 for the Havona order; 39:2.9).

rejected.reason: 'inteligencia' reads as intellect or espionage; here 'intelligence' is news

iran.name: Irán
iran.meaning: The Iranian plateau and its peoples, a corridor of Andite migration and land of Zoroaster (79:1, 95:6).

iroquois.name: iroqueses
iroquois.meaning: The federation of six nations of northern American red men, their nearest approach to a state (71:1.3).

isaac-old-testament.name: Isaac (Antiguo Testamento)
isaac-old-testament.meaning: The son of Abraham and Sarah, born after Melchizedek's promise (93:6.5, 93:9.8).

isaiah-first.name: Isaías (el primero)
isaiah-first.meaning: The first of the two Hebrew prophets named Isaiah; he appeared after an awakening of conscience in the Hebrew nations and preached a God of universal creation and upholding (97:5.1, 97:7.6).

rejected.reason: A term of biblical scholarship; the papers say 'the first Isaiah', a plain ordinal.

isaiah-second.name: Isaías (el segundo)
isaiah-second.meaning: The young prophet of the Babylonian captivity whose writings are chapters 40 to 55 of the book of Isaiah (97:7.4).

isis.name: Isis
isis.meaning: The Egyptian form of the goddess Ishtar (95:1.7).

islam.name: islam
islam.meaning: The monotheistic religion of the followers of Mohammed (also called Mohammedanism), the religio-cultural connective of North Africa, the Levant, and southeastern Asia (92:6.19, 5:4.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish writes religion names in lowercase, as in 'budismo' and 'cristianismo' in this glossary.

isle-of-paradise.name: Isla del Paraíso
isle-of-paradise.meaning: The stationary Isle at the heart of the central universe, the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (0:0.5).

rejected.reason: Reads as a resort name; Spanish needs the "de" link.

isle-of-patmos.name: isla de Patmos
isle-of-patmos.meaning: The Greek island where the apostle John was banished for four years and wrote the Book of Revelation (historical place).

rejected.reason: The capital on the generic noun is not the standard Spanish form for this historical place.

forcedChoices: lowercase "isla": Standard Spanish writes the generic geographic noun in lowercase before a historical place name.

italy.name: Italia
italy.meaning: The land to which Andites came from the Aegean islands (80:7.11).

jacob-s-well.name: pozo de Jacob
jacob-s-well.meaning: The well in Samaria on the route that Jews often avoided (124:6.1).

jacob-the-stone-mason-son.name: Jacob (hijo del cantero)
jacob-the-stone-mason-son.meaning: The neighbor boy, son of the stone mason, who appointed himself Jesus' defender in childhood (124:2.4, 133:1.5).

rejected.reason: Also a Spanish form, but 'Jacob' is the plain form of the Hebrew name.
'albañil' is a bricklayer, not a stone mason.

jairus.name: Jairo
jairus.meaning: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum whose only daughter Jesus went to heal (152:0.1, 153:1.7).

james-brother-of-jesus.name: Santiago (hermano de Jesús)
james-brother-of-jesus.meaning: James, the second-born brother of Jesus, later head of the church at Jerusalem.

rejected.reason: Also used in Spanish, but 'Santiago' matches the done term 'Santiago Zebedeo'.

james-zebedee.name: Santiago Zebedeo
james-zebedee.meaning: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the twelve and the first apostle martyred (139:3.1).

rejected.reason: Used in some Bibles, but 'Santiago' is the common Spanish name of this apostle across countries.

japan.name: Japón
japan.meaning: The island country of eastern Asia, named among regions of great crustal change (60:3.6).

jeremiah.name: Jeremías
jeremiah.meaning: The Hebrew prophet of the time of the siege of Jerusalem.

jericho.name: Jericó
jericho.meaning: The ancient city near the Jordan crossing that Jesus visited several times.

jerusalem.name: Jerusalén
jerusalem.meaning: The historical city of Palestine, earlier Salem and Jebus, center of Jewish worship with its temple, where Jesus taught and was crucified (Papers 121-187).

jerusalem-temple.name: templo de Jerusalén
jerusalem-temple.meaning: The temple at Jerusalem, center of Jewish worship and sacrifice, where Jesus taught (173:1.1).

jerusalem-temple-guards.name: guardias del templo de Jerusalén
jerusalem-temple-guards.meaning: The Jewish guards of the temple, who were on duty at Jesus' tomb with the Roman guard (189:1.2).

jerusem.name: Jerusem
jerusem.meaning: The headquarters world of the local system of Satania, encircled by fifty-six worlds of transition culture (47:0.1, 46:5.27).

jesus.name: Jesús
jesus.meaning: Jesus of Nazareth, the human life on Urantia of the Creator Son Michael of Nebadon (0:0.5, 194:3.1).

jews.name: judíos
jews.meaning: The Jewish people, descendants of the Hebrews (97:0.1, 121:2.1).

jews-ancient-hebrews.name: judíos (antiguos hebreos)
jews-ancient-hebrews.meaning: The ancient Hebrew people, Abraham's descendants together with adopted nomads, from whom the Jewish nation formed (Papers 96-97).

joanna.name: Juana
joanna.meaning: The wife of Chuza, steward of Herod Antipas, one of the ten women Jesus set apart for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

job-book.name: Job (libro)
job-book.meaning: The Old Testament book that reflects the teachings of the Salem school in Mesopotamia and shows that suffering is not always punishment for sin (95:1.10, 148:6.11).

john-mark.name: Juan Marcos
john-mark.meaning: John Mark, the boy of chores for Jesus and the apostles, later the writer of the Gospel of Mark (121:8.2, 177:2.1).

john-the-baptist.name: Juan el Bautista
john-the-baptist.meaning: John, son of Zacharias and Elizabeth, who preached repentance and baptized Jesus (135:0.1).

john-zebedee.name: Juan Zebedeo
john-zebedee.meaning: John, son of Zebedee, the youngest of the twelve apostles (139:4.1).

joppa.name: Jope
joppa.meaning: A port town on the Mediterranean coast of Palestine where Jesus met Gadiah the Philistine interpreter (130:1.1, 134:7.4).

rejected.reason: The modern name; the papers use the ancient name.

joseph-brother-of-jesus.name: José (hermano de Jesús)
joseph-brother-of-jesus.meaning: The fourth child of the Nazareth family, born March 16, A.D. 1 (123:4.9).

joseph-father-of-jesus.name: José (padre de Jesús)
joseph-father-of-jesus.meaning: Joseph, the human father of Jesus, a carpenter and builder of Nazareth who died in an accident when Jesus was fourteen (122:1.1, 126:2.2).

joseph-of-arimathea.name: José de Arimatea
joseph-of-arimathea.meaning: A wealthy member of the Sanhedrin and a believer who gave his tomb for the body of Jesus; his daughter Rebecca joined the women's corps (150:1.1).

joshua-old-testament.name: Josué (Antiguo Testamento)
joshua-old-testament.meaning: The leader of Israel after Moses who kept the Mosaic tradition of God while the common people reverted to the older desert idea of Yahweh (96:6.1).

josiah-blind-beggar.name: Josías (mendigo ciego)
josiah-blind-beggar.meaning: The blind man whom Jesus healed on a Sabbath in Jerusalem by the pool of Siloam, and who became a lifelong preacher of the gospel (164:3.8, 164:5.6, 171:5.1).

judaism.name: judaísmo
judaism.meaning: The religion of the Jews that grew from the Hebrew faith and held the concept of one God (97:0.1, 121:2.1).

judas-iscariot.name: Judas Iscariote
judas-iscariot.meaning: The Judean apostle, treasurer of the twelve, who betrayed Jesus (139:12.1).

jude.name: Judas (hermano de Jesús)
jude.meaning: Jude, the youngest brother of Jesus, of fiery and patriotic temper (127:1.6, 128:4.6).

rejected.reason: the name of the patriarch and the tribe
not a Spanish form

forcedChoices: Judas, with the qualifier: Spanish has one name for English 'Jude' and 'Judas'; the English keeps them apart

judea.name: Judea
judea.meaning: The southern region of Palestine, with Jerusalem.

jupiter-planet.name: Júpiter (planeta)
jupiter-planet.meaning: The giant planet of the solar system, formed with Saturn from the central portion of the matter that Angona pulled from the sun (57:5.9, 57:6.5).

justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.name: Justo (mercader judío de Corinto)
justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.meaning: A devout Jewish merchant of Corinth, living beside the synagogue, who often hosted Jesus and Ganid and later the Apostle Paul (133:3.5).

rejected.reason: Spanish gives Latin personal names in their Spanish form.

justus-jewish-merchant-of-corinth.note: "Justo" is also the common adjective "just". The capital and the qualifier must show that it is a name.

kc-absolute.name: absoluto
kc-absolute.meaning: Beginningless, endless, timeless, spaceless, and unconditioned; the third level of reality after the finite and the absonite (0:1.13, 0:11.12).

rejected.reason: 'Total' and 'totality' are separate words in the papers.
The reader must not read it as a mere intensifier ('un absoluto desastre').

kc-absonite.name: absonito
kc-absonite.meaning: The level of reality between the finite and the absolute, of things and beings without beginnings or endings that transcend time and space and are eventuated, not created (0:1.12, 0:9.2).

rejected.reason: Spanish needs an agreeing adjective; "absonito" and "absonita" follow the noun's gender.

kc-actualize.name: actualizar
kc-actualize.meaning: To pass from potential to actual existence, to bring into full expression what was only a capacity (0:4.1, 115:3.16, 117:2.9).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'realize' and 'realization' as separate words (115:3.16), and 'realizar' is also 'to do'.
Breaks the family with 'actual' and 'actualidad'.
The reader must not bring 'to update, to bring up to date'. The sense is the philosophical one, 'to put into act'.

kc-actualize.note: Family root 'act-': actual, actualidad, actualizar, beside potencial, potencialidad. The common Spanish sense 'update' is a risk.

kc-ascender.name: ascendente
kc-ascender.meaning: A creature of evolutionary origin who climbs from the material worlds toward Paradise (13:1.21, 20:1.1).

rejected.reason: Means an elevator.
The reader must not bring these; the sense is one who ascends. Matches 'mortales ascendentes'.

kc-ascension-career.name: carrera de ascensión
kc-ascension-career.meaning: The whole course of a creature's ascent from the material worlds to Paradise.

rejected.reason: Breaks the family root 'ascensión'.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) 'carrera' = a race or a university degree
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the sense is a course of life.

kc-associate.name: asociado
kc-associate.meaning: As noun, one who works together with another; as verb and adjective, joined in relation or function (0:1.6 'Associative Deity', 0:5.4, 8:0.4 'eternally associated persons').

rejected.reason: A business partner or a club member; a commercial sense.
Too informal and personal; loses the sense of joined function.
The reader must not bring the firm or law-office rank to it.

kc-co-ordinate.name: coordinar
kc-co-ordinate.meaning: As verb, to bring into unified and harmonious function; as adjective, equal in rank or status, as the three Paradise Deities are co-ordinate (7:7.1, 8:0.4, 42:12.13 'On Paradise the three energies are co-ordinate, in Havona co-ordinated').

rejected.reason: Mathematical 'co-ordinate' (axes); a false sense.
Explains the adjective and breaks the family with the verb, which 42:12.13 sets side by side.
As an adjective the reader must also take 'of equal rank', as in grammar ('oraciones coordinadas'), not only 'organized'.

kc-cosmic-insight.name: perspicacia cósmica
kc-cosmic-insight.meaning: A person's clear understanding of universe realities and his place among them, one of the values by which mortal progress through the cosmic circles is measured (106:0.1, 49:6.8, 100:4.2).

rejected.reason: 'Intuición' suggests knowledge without reasoning; 0:6.8 calls insight intellectual.
Collides with 'spiritual vision', which 100:4.2 sets beside cosmic insight.
Shares the root with 'Discernidores de Espíritus'.

kc-creator-creature.name: Creador-criatura
kc-creator-creature.meaning: The relationship and shared experience between Creator and created being, which the papers compare to the Father-child affection and which the Supreme personifies (3:4.7, 21:3.23, 117:1.1).

rejected.reason: 'creatura' is a Latinism, not current Spanish.

kc-enseraphimed.name: enserafinado
kc-enseraphimed.meaning: Enclosed in a transport seraphim for travel through space, in transit sleep (39:2.12, 39:5.14, 51:2.2).

rejected.reason: mixes English spelling into a Spanish verb form
plain paraphrase; the English coins one word

kc-evolutionary.name: evolutivo
kc-evolutionary.meaning: Of time-space creatures and realms that grow and progress through experience from lower to higher states, as against existential or Paradise origin (0:1.18, 0:5.1, 16:4.1).

rejected.reason: Anglicism, not standard Spanish.
Means 'a supporter of the theory of evolution', an ideological sense.

kc-existential.name: existencial
kc-existential.meaning: Eternal and without origin, existing by nature rather than through experience, as the Paradise Deities are; the opposite of experiential (0:1.14, 0:1.18, 0:4.9, 0:7.5).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the sense of existentialist philosophy or personal anguish ("crisis existencial").
Too broad; the Supreme is eternal in future but not existential (0:9.5).

kc-finite.name: finito
kc-finite.meaning: The level of reality of creature life and time-space limitations; finite realities always have beginnings (0:1.11).

rejected.reason: Plain 'limited'; loses the technical level set against 'absonite' and 'absolute'.

kc-guardian-of-destiny.name: guardián del destino
kc-guardian-of-destiny.meaning: The personal seraphim assigned to a mortal who reaches the third psychic circle, who keeps the life record and accompanies the survivor (110:6.14, 113:2.2, 112:4.12).

rejected.reason: carries the popular Catholic belief of a guardian from birth; the papers assign it at the third circle
the papers write 'her' for the seraphim, but the noun 'serafín' is masculine

forcedChoices: masculine 'guardián': agrees with 'serafín'; the papers use 'her', so a translator can keep feminine pronouns in the sentence

kc-indwelling.name: morada interior
kc-indwelling.meaning: The dwelling of a divine spirit (above all the Thought Adjuster) within the mind of a mortal; as adjective, 'the indwelling spirit' is the spirit that lives within (0:5.9, 0:5.10, 34:6.7).

rejected.reason: A technical term of Christian theology for the Holy Spirit in the soul; a religious sense the authors did not set.
Reads as a home address or a legal residence permit.

kc-infinite.name: infinito
kc-infinite.meaning: Without limit; the fullness implied by the primacy of the First Source and Center; 'the Infinite' (capital) is the Father-Infinite (0:3.24, 0:1).

rejected.reason: Plain 'unlimited'; loses the technical level of 'infinite' set against 'finite' and 'absolute'.

kc-isle.name: Isla
kc-isle.meaning: The Isle is Paradise as a stationary, material-like body at the center of all things, the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of God (0:0.5, 11:2.8, 105:3.4).

rejected.reason: Literary and archaic; the English uses the plain word.
Means a small island; the Isle is immense.

kc-mortal.name: mortal
kc-mortal.meaning: A will creature of material, evolutionary origin who is subject to physical death, and who can survive it by the soul (0:5.10, 40:9.1).

rejected.reason: Too narrow: the papers apply 'mortal' to will creatures on many worlds, not only to Urantia humans.
As an adjective Spanish 'mortal' also means 'deadly' (herida mortal, pecado mortal); the reader must not bring this sense to 'mente mortal' or 'vida mortal'.

kc-paradise-deity.name: Deidad del Paraíso
kc-paradise-deity.meaning: The existential Deity of Paradise, existing as three persons in the Paradise Trinity, as distinct from the experiential Deities that are still emerging (0:4.9, 0:7.7, 0:7.9).

rejected.reason: 'divinity' is a separate term (the quality of Deity); the two must stay distinct.

kc-perfecting.name: en perfeccionamiento
kc-perfecting.meaning: In the process of becoming perfect by evolutionary growth in time, as the superuniverses and evolutionary creatures are, in contrast to the perfect (Havona) and the perfected (32:3.14, 105:6.5, 106:1.1, 117:1.2).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'that makes something perfect' (active cause), not 'that is becoming perfect'.
Loses the idea of progress toward perfection.
Correct sense but long; kept as a possible paraphrase, not the term.

forcedChoices: adjectival phrase 'en perfeccionamiento' or relative clause 'que se perfecciona': Spanish has no one-word participle adjective with the ongoing sense of English 'perfecting'.

kc-personality-survival.name: supervivencia de la personalidad
kc-personality-survival.meaning: The survival of the personality, held by the soul and the Adjuster, past the death of the body (112:2, 112:5).

kc-prepersonal.name: prepersonal
kc-prepersonal.meaning: Of a reality that is not yet a personality but is destined to become part of one, as the Thought Adjuster (0:5.9, 0:1.3, 0:5.4).

rejected.reason: Explains and loses the term.

kc-progression.name: progresión
kc-progression.meaning: The step-by-step advance of a creature through levels of attainment, as in the circles of mortal progression and the routes of progression to Paradise (49:6.8, 40:3.1).

rejected.reason: Plainer, but reserved for the separate English word 'progress', which the papers also use (49:6.8).
The reader must not bring this.

kc-sonship.name: filiación
kc-sonship.meaning: The status of being a son of God, which a person knows and grasps by faith (140:10.9, 193:0.4, 196:3.34).

rejected.reason: Correct but long; a phrase where the English uses one word.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) 'filiación' = political membership or personal data on a record
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the sense is the relation of a son to his father.

kc-spirit-born.name: nacido del espíritu
kc-spirit-born.meaning: Said of a mortal or a soul that has been born of the spirit, that is, has received and recognized the indwelling of God and lives under spirit leading (34:6.7, 34:6.13, 193:2.2, 42:12.12).

rejected.reason: Brings the evangelical 'born-again' label, a cultural sense the authors do not use.
The capital would decide that the spirit is the Spirit (a person); the English lowercase compound leaves this open, so the lowercase stays.

kc-spirit-luminosity.name: luminosidad espiritual
kc-spirit-luminosity.meaning: The 'light' that is the personality manifestation of spirit beings; a figure of speech, not related to intellectual insight or to physical light (0:6.8, 0:6.9).

rejected.reason: 'Luz' is the papers' 'light', the general word of which 'spirit luminosity' is one of three kinds (0:6.8).
Can read as the brightness of a person's mood or wit; 'espiritual' marks the spirit level better.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) the 'spiritual glow' of a saintly person
rejected.reason: The reader must not take it as a religious aura or a holy look; the papers make it a manifestation of spirit beings.

kc-spiritual.name: espiritual
kc-spiritual.meaning: Of or pertaining to spirit: that which responds to the spirit circuit of the Eternal Son and to the spirit level of reality, as against the material and the mindal (0:6.1, 0:6.2, 42:12.13).

rejected.reason: Means 'spiritist' (contact with the dead) or a philosophical school; a sense the authors do not intend.
The reader must not read it as a mood or a personal temperament; in the papers it names a level of reality.

kc-superconscious.name: superconsciente
kc-superconscious.meaning: The levels of the human mind above ordinary consciousness, the domain where the Thought Adjuster makes contact and where religious growth takes place (100:1.9, 91:2.6, 91:3.5).

rejected.reason: Also valid Spanish, but 'super-' matches 'superpersonal' and 'superuniversos'.
The papers set the superconscious against the subconscious (91:3.5).

kc-superhuman.name: sobrehumano
kc-superhuman.meaning: Above the human level, as beings, wisdom, or help from orders higher than mortals (for example the midwayers and the revelators).

rejected.reason: Less standard than "sobrehumano"; the English uses a common word.
The reader must not bring the sense "enormous effort" ("un esfuerzo sobrehumano").

kc-supermaterial.name: supermaterial
kc-supermaterial.meaning: Above the material level of reality: the morontial, mind, and spirit levels on which Deity shows its unity (0:1.2).

rejected.reason: Not a current Spanish word; "super-" follows the glossary (superpersonal, superuniversos).
Means only "not material"; loses "above".

kc-superpersonal.name: superpersonal
kc-superpersonal.meaning: Of a reality above the level of personality as creatures know it, as Deity functions superpersonally (0:1.2, 0:1.3, 0:5.4).

rejected.reason: Breaks the 'super-' family of the papers (superuniverso, superpersonal).

kc-supreme-being.name: Ser Supremo
kc-supreme-being.meaning: The evolving experiential Deity that unifies the sevenfold manifestation of Deity in the grand universe as one Lord, the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite (0:7.7, 0:7.8, 0:7.9).

rejected.reason: Kept the form, but the reader must not take it as a generic name for God; here it names an evolving Deity distinct from the Universal Father.

kc-totality.name: totalidad
kc-totality.meaning: The whole of something taken all together, as the totality of cosmic reality or of the co-ordinated infinite nature of God (1:5.13, 10:4.6, 42:2.3).

rejected.reason: Means a set or a group; loses the sense of the complete whole.

kc-transcendental.name: trascendental
kc-transcendental.meaning: Belonging to the absonite level that transcends time and space, between finite and absolute (0:9.1, 0:9.5, 0:2.17).

rejected.reason: Valid but less common than "trascendental" in current Spanish.
The reader must not bring the sense "very important" or the sense of Kantian philosophy.

kc-triodity.name: triodidad
kc-triodity.meaning: A non-Father triune relationship, such as the triodity of actuality or of potentiality, consequent on the triunities (104:5.1, 115:3.7).

rejected.reason: Ordinary sense is an electronic valve.

kc-ultimate.name: último
kc-ultimate.meaning: In its special sense, pertaining to the absonite level of Deity and reality that transcends time and space, the second level of experiential divinity after the supreme (0:1.10, 0:1.12, 0:9.2); in many other uses it keeps its ordinary English sense of final or fundamental.

rejected.reason: Means only 'at the end'; loses the sense of a level beyond time and space and breaks the family with Ultimidad.
Not a Spanish word; reads as a coinage where the English uses a plain word.
Kept the word, but the reader must not bring the sense 'the last one'; the intended sense is the philosophical 'fundamental, beyond' as in 'realidad última'.

kenites.name: quenitas
kenites.meaning: A people with whom the line of Abraham through Isaac intermarried, the only line that long kept a clear concept of the Salem teachings (93:10.3).

rejected.reason: Also a standard Spanish form; 'quenitas' follows the -ita pattern of the done terms (Anditas, Noditas).

kheresa.name: Kheresa
kheresa.meaning: The fishing village by the Sea of Galilee, home of the Alpheus twins, where Jesus called them (138:4.1).

kidron.name: Cedrón
kidron.meaning: The brook and valley beside Jerusalem near Gethsemane and the Mount of Olives (142:8.4, 176:0.2).

kingdom-of-heaven.name: reino de los cielos
kingdom-of-heaven.meaning: In Jesus' teaching, the spiritual rule of God that consists in recognizing God's sovereignty, believing in sonship with God, and having faith in the desire to do his will (140:10.9).

rejected.reason: Literal, but less natural; the plural is the ordinary Spanish phrase for this gospel term.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) a political kingdom or a place after death
rejected.reason: The reader must not bring these; the papers present a spiritual rule in human hearts.

lanaforge.name: Lanaforge
lanaforge.meaning: The present System Sovereign of Satania, successor of Lucifer, the only primary Lanonandek in Nebadon who stayed loyal when his superior fell (45:2.2, 45:2.3).

lanonandek-sons.name: Hijos Lanonandek
lanonandek-sons.meaning: The third order of local universe Sons, created by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, who serve as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes (35:8).

lao-tse.name: Lao-Tse
lao-tse.meaning: The Chinese teacher of the sixth century B.C. who envisioned more of God in Tao than Confucius did in humanity (92:5.12).

rejected.reason: Pinyin form; the papers use the older form Lao-tse.

lazarus-of-bethany.name: Lázaro (de Betania)
lazarus-of-bethany.meaning: Jesus' friend at Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, whom Jesus raised from the dead (Paper 168).

lemurs.name: lémures
lemurs.meaning: The lemur family whose early ancestors appeared in western North America and from whose types the dawn mammals came (61:2.10, 61:6.1).

rejected.reason: In Spanish 'lémures' is also the Roman spirits of the dead; the context must show the animal.

life-carriers.name: Portadores de Vida
life-carriers.meaning: Local universe Sons who design life, carry it to the planets, plant it, and foster its development (36:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Transportador' reads as freight or a machine.
Correct, but the article makes it read less as a term; the English has no article.

light-and-life.name: luz y vida
light-and-life.meaning: The settled status of an inhabited world, the evolutionary goal of all mortal-inhabited worlds of the present age, reached after the Daynal Sons' missions (20:9.4, 36:1.4, 55:0.1).

rejected.reason: The hyphenated form is only an adjective in English; Spanish uses "de luz y vida".

local-systems.name: sistemas locales
local-systems.meaning: Units of about one thousand inhabited worlds under a System Sovereign; Satania is Urantia's system (15:2.3, 32:2.11).

local-universe-centers.name: centros de los universos locales
local-universe-centers.meaning: The fourth order of Supreme Power Centers, stationed on local universe headquarters, which downstep superuniverse power for constellations and systems (29:2).

local-universe-mother-spirit-of-nebadon.name: Espíritu Madre del universo local de Nebadon
aliases: Espíritus Madre de los universos locales
local-universe-mother-spirit-of-nebadon.meaning: The Creative Spirit who is co-director with Michael of Nebadon, known as the Divine Minister of Salvington, whose personal influence is the Holy Spirit and who never leaves Salvington (34:4.7).
forcedChoices: feminine "Ministra Divina": The papers refer to the Mother Spirit as "she" (34:4.7).

local-universe-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre de los universos locales
aliases: Espíritus Creativos de los Universos Locales
Espíritu Madre de un universo local
local-universe-mother-spirits.meaning: The individualized representation of the Infinite Spirit who joins each Creator Son to organize, create, and minister in a local universe; the adjutants are her children (34:0.1, 36:5.1).

rejected.reason: In Spanish a noun in apposition stays singular ('Espíritus Madre'), as in other compound names.
'Creador' is the translation of 'Creator' (Creator Sons); 'Creative' is a different English word, so it gets 'Creativo'.
The papers refer to the Mother Spirit as 'her'; the feminine 'Ministra' agrees.

local-universe-power-centers.name: centros de poder de los universos locales
local-universe-power-centers.meaning: Fourth-order Supreme Power Centers on local universe headquarters, which modify and distribute superuniverse power (29:2).

local-universe-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios del Universo Local
local-universe-sons-of-god.meaning: The orders of divine sonship native to or serving in a local universe, such as Melchizedeks, Vorondadeks, and Lanonandeks (35:0).

local-universes.name: universos locales
local-universes.meaning: The creations of the Creator Sons, each of one hundred constellations of one hundred systems of inhabited worlds (32:0.1).

lord-s-prayer.name: Oración del Señor
lord-s-prayer.meaning: The prayer that Jesus first formed at fifteen for his family and later taught his apostles, which many came to call the Lord's Prayer (126:3.3, 144:3.15).

rejected.reason: The usual Spanish name, but it names the prayer by its first words; the English names it by its giver and quotes the name as a popular label (126:3.3). Kept as an alias.

lot.name: Lot
lot.meaning: Abraham's nephew, who went with him to Salem (93:5.5).

lucifer.name: Lucifer
lucifer.meaning: A primary Lanonandek Son, once System Sovereign of Satania, who led a rebellion against Michael and the Father (53:1).

rejected.reason: A traditional Spanish name with a folk-religious sense; the English uses "Lucifer".

lucifer-rebellion.name: rebelión de Lucifer
lucifer-rebellion.meaning: The revolt of Lucifer, System Sovereign of Satania, against the universe plan and the rule of Michael (53:0.1, 53:3.6).

luke.name: Lucas
luke.meaning: The physician of Antioch in Pisidia, a gentile convert of Paul, who wrote the Gospel by Luke and Acts (121:8.8).

lutentia.name: Lutentia
lutentia.meaning: A rebel Lanonandek System Sovereign in Nebadon whom the Most Highs deposed and whom Michael replaced during his second bestowal (119:2.2, 119:2.4).

maccabees.name: Macabeos
maccabees.meaning: The Jewish family and movement of the Maccabean revolt, with which Mary's ancestors were identified; also the name of a book (122:5.10, 121:6.3).

machiventa-melchizedek.name: Machiventa Melquisedec
machiventa-melchizedek.meaning: The Melchizedek Son who incarnated at Salem as an emergency bestowal, taught Abraham, and is now vicegerent Planetary Prince of Urantia (93:1.2, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: The biblical name has a standard Spanish form, and 'Hijos Melquisedec' is already done.

magadan-park.name: parque de Magadán
magadan-park.meaning: The park near Bethsaida-Julias where Jesus and the apostles camped and held conferences, and where the five thousand gathered (157:2.1, 152:2.4).

magdala.name: Magdala
magdala.meaning: The town by the Sea of Galilee where the women evangelists first worked and where Mary Magdalene was won for the kingdom (150:2.2).

magisterial-sons.name: Hijos Magistrales
magisterial-sons.meaning: The secondary Paradise Sons, offspring of the Eternal Son and the Infinite Spirit (Avonals), who judge dispensations on the worlds and also bestow themselves as mortals (20:1.11, 20:5.6, 20:6.5).

rejected.reason: 'Magisterial' in Spanish means of teachers or of a magistracy and is also a church term (magisterio); 'magistral' keeps the sense of authority and judgment.
Narrows them to judges and loses the adjective form of the English.

majeston.name: Majeston
majeston.meaning: The chief of reflectivity, personalized by a reaction of the Deity Absolute after the forty-ninth Reflective Spirit; the Paradise center of all reflectivity, where the mind of the Supreme focuses as a time-space experience (17:2.2, 0:3.14).

major-sectors.name: sectores mayores
major-sectors.meaning: About one tenth of a superuniverse: one hundred minor sectors and ten thousand local universes, ruled by three Perfections of Days (15:13.1).

manotia.name: Manotia
manotia.meaning: A supreme seraphim who achieved all seven seraphic services, was second in command of the Satania seraphim in the Lucifer rebellion, and is now associate chief of seraphim on Urantia (39:0.9, 53:6.1).

mansion-world-students.name: estudiantes de los mundos morada
mansion-world-students.meaning: All surviving mortals who reawaken on the mansion worlds, as one class of ascending mortals (30:4.14, 47:3.9).

mansion-world-teachers.name: Instructores de los Mundos Morada
mansion-world-teachers.meaning: Glorified cherubim and sanobim who, after the embrace of the Universe Mother Spirit, teach on the mansion worlds and higher educational spheres (48:5.2).

rejected.reason: 'Maestros' is already 'Master' (Hijos Maestros); 'Teacher' is 'Instructor' as in 'Hijos Instructores de la Trinidad'.

mansion-worlds.name: mundos morada
mansion-worlds.meaning: The seven satellites of the first transition world of Jerusem, where surviving mortals first reawaken; the name refers to Jesus' saying about 'many mansions in the Father's universe' (47:0.1, 30:4.14).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'mansión' means a luxurious house; the papers mean dwelling places, as in the saying of Jesus.
Same luxury sense, and longer.
Reads as a ranch or a short stay; loses the link to the saying.

mansions.name: moradas
mansions.meaning: The training worlds of mortal residence, of which Jesus said "In my Father's house are many mansions" (30:4.17, 47:0.1).

rejected.reason: Spanish "mansión" suggests a luxury house; "morada" also keeps the family with "mundos morada".

martha-sister-of-jesus.name: Marta (hermana de Jesús)
martha-sister-of-jesus.meaning: Jesus' second sister, born September 13 in A.D. 3, who became an expert weaver (124:1.7, 128:3.1).

martha-sister-of-lazarus.name: Marta (hermana de Lázaro)
martha-sister-of-lazarus.meaning: The sister of Lazarus and Mary of Bethany, later in Philadelphia with them (190:1.10).

mary-magdalene.name: María Magdalena
mary-magdalene.meaning: The woman of Magdala, leader among the women evangelists, first to see the risen Jesus (Papers 150, 189-190).

mary-mother-of-jesus.name: María (madre de Jesús)
mary-mother-of-jesus.meaning: Mary, the earthly mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph (122:1.2).

mary-sister-of-lazarus.name: María (hermana de Lázaro)
mary-sister-of-lazarus.meaning: The sister of Lazarus and Martha of Bethany, who went to Philadelphia with them (190:1.10).

master-architects.name: Arquitectos Maestros
master-architects.meaning: The short name of the Architects of the Master Universe (31:9.1).

master-force-organizers.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza
aliases: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso
master-force-organizers.meaning: Transcendental beings who work with space potency and organize the nebulae (29:5.1, 42:2.8).

master-mathematician.name: Matemático Maestro
master-mathematician.meaning: A phrase for the mind behind the mathematical order of the universe, used against materialism (195:6.8); the text does not name a specific being.

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family

master-michaels.name: Migueles Maestros
master-michaels.meaning: Creator Sons (Michaels) who, settled in supreme authority after their sevenfold bestowal, rule their universes with unlimited power derived from experienced association with the Paradise Trinity (21:0.3, 21:5.1).

rejected.reason: The name is already 'Miguel' in 'Miguel de Nebadon'; the family must keep one root.
Spanish puts the qualifier after the noun, as in 'Hijos Maestros'.

master-physical-controllers.name: Controladores Físicos Maestros
master-physical-controllers.meaning: The mobile subordinates of the Supreme Power Centers who control physical energies and travel fast through local space (29:4.1, 41:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Maestro' before the noun reads as a teacher of controllers; after the noun it means principal, as in 'Espíritus Maestros'.

master-seraphim-of-planetary-supervision.name: serafines maestros de la supervisión planetaria
master-seraphim-of-planetary-supervision.meaning: Twelve corps of completion seraphim from Seraphington who supervise planetary affairs under the resident governor general (114:6.1, 39:9.2).

rejected.reason: breaks the 'master' family (Maestro)

master-sons.name: Hijos Maestros
master-sons.meaning: Creator Sons who completed their seven bestowals and so earned full sovereignty of their universe (21:4.6, 21:5.6).

rejected.reason: interprets; the English says 'Master'

master-spirit-number-five.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Cinco
master-spirit-number-five.meaning: The Master Spirit who blends the character of the Father and the Infinite Spirit (16:3.10).

master-spirit-number-four.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Cuatro
master-spirit-number-four.meaning: The Master Spirit who combines the natures of the Father and the Son (16:3.8).

master-spirit-number-one.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Uno
master-spirit-number-one.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially represents the Universal Father (16:3.2).

master-spirit-number-seven.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Siete
master-spirit-number-seven.meaning: The Master Spirit who represents the Father, Son, and Spirit together and speaks for the Supreme Being (16:3.15).

master-spirit-number-six.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Seis
master-spirit-number-six.meaning: The Master Spirit who portrays the combined character of the Son and the Spirit (16:3.12).

master-spirit-number-three.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Tres
master-spirit-number-three.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially resembles the Infinite Spirit (16:3.6).

master-spirit-number-two.name: Espíritu Maestro Número Dos
master-spirit-number-two.meaning: The Master Spirit who especially portrays the Eternal Son (16:3.4).

master-spirits-seven.name: Espíritus Maestros, Siete
master-spirits-seven.meaning: The seven primary personalities of the Infinite Spirit, one for each superuniverse, who represent all seven possible associations of the three Deities (16:0.1, 15:0.1).

rejected.reason: Adds the idea of governing; 'Master' here means primary or chief, which 'maestro' as an adjective carries (as in 'plan maestro').
Plain adjective; does not read as a term and breaks one word, one translation with Master Physical Controllers.

master-universe.name: universo maestro
master-universe.meaning: All of the creation in space: the grand universe plus the uninhabited but mobilizing universes of outer space (0:0.6, 12:1).

rejected.reason: Suggests one universe among others; loses the sense of the all-inclusive whole.
The reader must not bring the sense "teacher"; "maestro" follows "Espíritus Maestros" in the glossary.

matadormus.name: Matadormus
matadormus.meaning: The rich young member of the Jerusalem Sanhedrin who asked Jesus for ordination and about eternal life (163:2.4).

material-sons.name: Hijos Materiales
material-sons.meaning: The order of Sons sent in pairs, as Adam and Eve, to uplift the races of an evolutionary world biologically (51:0.1).

matthew-levi.name: Mateo Leví
matthew-levi.meaning: Matthew Levi, the seventh apostle, a former customs collector of Capernaum and the apostolic treasurer (139:7.1).

meanings.name: significados
meanings.meaning: The "mind meanings" of reality, the understanding that mind adds to perception of things, set between things (energy) and values (spirit) (0:0.3, 0:1.1, 0:4.10).

rejected.reason: Also the five senses and directions; ambiguous.
Heavier "-ción" noun with no gain.

mechanical-controllers.name: controladores mecánicos
mechanical-controllers.meaning: The most powerful Master Physical Controllers on inhabited worlds, with a living antigravity endowment; ten on Urantia help seraphic transports depart (29:4.19).

mediterranean-region.name: región mediterránea
mediterranean-region.meaning: The region around the Mediterranean Sea, where races from the north, south, and east met and mixed.

mediterranean-sea.name: mar Mediterráneo
mediterranean-sea.meaning: The sea that became one with the Atlantic when an earthquake broke the Gibraltar isthmus, causing the greatest loss of life by flood in history (80:2.4).

melchizedek-brotherhood.name: hermandad de Melquisedec
melchizedek-brotherhood.meaning: The group of believers in one God that Machiventa Melchizedek founded at Salem (93).

rejected.reason: 'Fraternidad' is used for 'brotherhood' as a quality (the brotherhood of man); 'hermandad' fits an organized body.
Ordinary sense is a Catholic lay confraternity.

forcedChoices: 'de Melquisedec' (person) rather than invariable 'Melquisedec' (order): The context is the Salem group of Machiventa.

melchizedek-college-of-administration.name: Colegio Melquisedec de Administración
melchizedek-college-of-administration.meaning: The school on Jerusem from which representatives and electors must graduate before they serve in system government (45:7).

rejected.reason: Acceptable; 'Colegio' keeps the English word, but in some countries it means a secondary school.

melchizedek-college-of-spiritual-endowme.name: Colegio Melquisedec de Dotación Espiritual
melchizedek-college-of-spiritual-endowme.meaning: A school of the Melchizedek University where Sons of God and seraphim train evangels of spiritual liberty and divine sonship.

rejected.reason: 'Dones' suggests charismatic gifts; 'endowment' is an endowing.

melchizedek-father.name: Melquisedec, Padre
melchizedek-father.meaning: The index form of Father Melchizedek, the first Melchizedek of Nebadon (93:1.2).

melchizedek-manovandet.name: Melquisedec, Manovandet
melchizedek-manovandet.meaning: A Melchizedek once attached to the receivership of Urantia, who presented Paper 53.

melchizedek-mantutia.name: Melquisedec, Mantutia
melchizedek-mantutia.meaning: The Melchizedek who directed the commission that presented Parts II and III and supervised the restatement in Paper 120.

melchizedek-receivers.name: síndicos Melquisedec
melchizedek-receivers.meaning: The twelve Melchizedeks who administered Urantia as custodians in trust after the Caligastia rebellion, until Michael's bestowal (67:6.5, 93:1.2, 93:9.11).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'receptor' means one who receives.
Loses the legal sense of receivership (custody of a forfeited estate).
Means holders of a deposit; weak sense of governing.

forcedChoices: 'síndicos': It carries the legal sense of receivership, but in some countries it also means a town official or a building manager; a human must confirm.

melchizedek-sons.name: Hijos Melquisedec
melchizedek-sons.meaning: An order of local universe Sons who serve as teachers, advisers, and emergency ministers; Machiventa Melchizedek of Salem was one of them (35:0.1, 49:0.1, 45:6.8).

rejected.reason: The name also belongs to the Melchizedek of Genesis, so the standard Spanish spelling 'Melquisedec' applies (rule for historical names). Reviewer can check this choice.
'de' makes them the children of one person; the name is the name of the order.

melchizedek-sphere.name: esfera Melquisedec
melchizedek-sphere.meaning: The pilot world of the Salvington circuit, headquarters of the Melchizedeks and site of Michael's first bestowal.

rejected.reason: Suggests one person; the English names the order.

melchizedek-university.name: Universidad Melquisedec
melchizedek-university.meaning: The training system of 490 worlds in the Salvington circuit where ascending mortals prepare for residence on Salvington.

melchizedek-worlds.name: mundos Melquisedec
melchizedek-worlds.meaning: The 490 worlds of the Salvington circuit that make up the Melchizedek University.

memories-of-mercy.name: Memorias de la Misericordia
memories-of-mercy.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim who are the living record of the mercy shown to each person, read in the courts of Uversa, and who teach ascenders to be truly merciful (28:6.6, 28:6.8).

rejected.reason: "recuerdo" is a single memory or a keepsake; the order is a living record.

memories-of-mercy.note: Plural "memorias" can also mean memoirs or a written report. The sense of a living record must come from the context.

merchant-of-damascus.name: mercader de Damasco
merchant-of-damascus.meaning: A wealthy part-Jewish merchant with caravans throughout the Roman world who befriended Jesus and later proposed that he head a school of religious philosophy at Damascus (128:3.3, 128:4.1).

mesopotamia.name: Mesopotamia
mesopotamia.meaning: The land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, the site of the second garden and of the Andite civilization (76:0.1, 78:1.1).

messenger-corps-david-zebedee-s.name: cuerpo de mensajeros (de David Zebedeo)
messenger-corps-david-zebedee-s.meaning: The group of runners organized by David Zebedee who carried news between Jesus, the apostles, and the believers, and who later helped him run the camps (163:5.2, 163:5.3).

messiah.name: Mesías
messiah.meaning: The anointed deliverer that the Jews expected, a hope that Jesus did not fulfill in the temporal sense (136:1.1).

mexico.name: México

michael-memorial-on-1st-mansion-world.name: monumento a Miguel (en el primer mundo morada)

michael-memorial-on-jerusem.meaning: A temple at the center of the circular reservations of the Sons on Jerusem, completed some five hundred years ago, now the center of the system management changed by Michael's bestowal, with a staff of over one million (46:5.19).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'memorial' first means a written petition; the papers call it a temple.

michael-of-nebadon.name: Miguel de Nebadon

michael-sons.name: Hijos Miguel
michael-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons of the order of Michael, the primary Paradise Sons who make the sevenfold bestowal (34:3.5, 20:5.2, 26:8.1).

michael-the-original.name: Miguel (el original)

midsoniters.name: midsonitarios

midspace-zones.name: zonas del espacio intermedio

zona del espacio de relativa quietud
midspace-zones.meaning: Relatively quiet elliptical regions of quiescent space activity that separate the successive space levels and separate pervaded from unpervaded space; near Paradise they are the transition zones from time to eternity (11:7.3, 11:7.7, 12:5.4).

rejected.reason: Not a natural Spanish word.

rejected.form: zonas intermedias (alone as the main name)

midway-messengers.name: mensajeros intermedios
midway-messengers.meaning: A small named group of the United Midwayers who give quick and reliable personal communication service on an evolutionary world (77:8.6).

rejected.reason: Reads as messengers who serve the midwayers, not midwayers who are messengers.

midwayers.name: seres intermedios
midwayers.meaning: Beings who live on a level about midway between mortals and the angelic orders, hence called midway creatures (77:0.1).

midwayers-chief-of-urantia.name: jefe de los seres intermedios de Urantia

midwayers-chief-of-urantia.meaning: The leader of the midwayers of Urantia, who presented Paper 91 on prayer (91:9.9, 77:8.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as a middle-rank chief, not the chief of the midwayers.

midwayers-primary.name: seres intermedios primarios
midwayers-primary.meaning: The first order of midway creatures, derived from the corporeal staff of the Planetary Prince, nearer to angels in nature, who serve as the planetary intelligence corps (38:9.9, 38:9.10, 77:1).

rejected.reason: Go-between sense; see secondary midwayers.

midwayers-secondary.name: seres intermedios secundarios

mighty-messengers.name: Mensajeros Poderosos
mighty-messengers.meaning: Trinity-embraced ascendant mortals, tested in rebellion, who serve in superuniverse administration (22:2.1).

rejected.reason: preposed adjective reads as praise, not as a name

milky-way-galaxy.name: galaxia de la Vía Láctea
milky-way-galaxy.meaning: The vast starry system that the papers call the central nucleus of the superuniverse of Orvonton (15:3.1, 15:3.2).

mind.name: mente

mind-energy-manipulators.name: manipuladores de energía mental

mind-personalities.name: personalidades de mente
mind-personalities.meaning: Unrevealed orders of beings dominated by mind but always associated with spirit, of which Majeston and his associates are an illustration (30:1.113).

rejected.reason: 'Mental' can suggest a psychological type or a mental illness.

mind-planners.name: planificadores de la mente

mindal-and-physical-energy-personalities.meaning: Unrevealed creatures that do not respond to spirit gravity but are true personalities within the Father's circuit (30:1.113).

rejected.reason: Drops 'energy', which is the point of the term.

minor-sectors.name: sectores menores
minor-sectors.meaning: A division of a superuniverse of one hundred local universes, ruled by three Recents of Days and mainly concerned with physical problems (15:2.6, 18:5.4).

miriam-sister-of-jesus.name: Miriam (hermana de Jesús)
miriam-sister-of-jesus.meaning: The eldest daughter of Joseph and Mary, sister of Jesus, who later married Jacob the stone mason (127:5.1, 128:5.8).

rejected.reason: Would merge her with Mary her mother and other Marys in the text.

mithraism.name: mitraísmo
mithraism.meaning: The greatest of the mystery cults, the worship of Mithras, spread over the Roman Empire by legions recruited in the Levant (98:5.1).

monmatia.name: Monmatia
monmatia.meaning: The name of Urantia's solar system (57:5).

monotheism.name: monoteísmo
monotheism.meaning: The belief in one God, as taught by Moses and held by the Hebrews and the Muslims (92:5.11, 104:1.9).

moon-urantia-s.name: luna (de Urantia)
moon-urantia-s.meaning: The satellite of Urantia, which in the far future will come near the earth and break into particles that form rings or fall as meteors (57:6.3).

morality.name: moralidad
morality.meaning: The recognition of duty and of right and wrong, a superanimal but subspiritual level of mind that prepares for religious experience.

rejected.reason: As a noun it also means morale (spirit of a group); kept only as an adjective alias.

morontia.name: morontia
morontia.meaning: The level of reality between the material and the spiritual, the substance of the soul and of the ascension life in the local universe (0:5.10, 103:6.7).

rejected.reason: Describes rather than names, and implies half spirit, which the papers do not say.

morontia-cherubim.name: querubines morontiales
morontia-cherubim.meaning: The 'fourth creatures' among cherubim and sanobim, who keep quasi-material traits and serve on the morontia training worlds (38:7.7, 38:8.4, 48:3.4).

morontia-companions.name: Compañeros Morontiales
morontia-companions.meaning: Beings of the local universe who act as hosts, guides, teachers of language, and interpreters for ascenders on the morontia worlds (48:3.4, 48:3.13).

morontia-counselors.name: consejeros morontiales
morontia-counselors.meaning: The seraphic transition ministers who teach mota on the mansion worlds to bring material and morontial viewpoints into focus (48:6.28).

rejected.reason: 'Asesor' reads as a technical adviser; also matches 'Consejeros Divinos'.

morontia-planners.name: planificadores morontiales
morontia-planners.meaning: Divine Builders among the celestial artisans who build for the co-ordinate association of all personalities present on a sphere (44:3.7).

morontia-power-supervisors.name: Supervisores del Poder Morontial

morontia-progressors.name: progresores morontiales

morontia-synthesizers.name: sintetizadores morontiales
morontia-synthesizers.meaning: Master artisans who add the finishing touches to morontia ensembles of beauty (44).

morontia-temple.name: templo morontial

morontia-world-transition-ministers.meaning: The sixth order of seraphim, who help mortals pass from the life in the flesh into morontia existence on the mansion worlds (48:6.1).

morontia-worlds.name: mundos morontiales

morontians.name: morontianos

mortal-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios Mortales

most-high-assistants.name: Asistentes Altísimos

mount-sinai.name: monte Sinaí

nathaniel-apostle.name: Natanael (apóstol)
nathaniel-apostle.meaning: Nathaniel of Cana, the sixth apostle, brought to Jesus by Philip (139:6.1).

nebadon.name: Nebadon

nicodemus.name: Nicodemo

nodites.name: Noditas

north-america.name: América del Norte

old-testament.name: Antiguo Testamento

omniaphim.name: omniafines

onagar.name: Onagar

orvonton-superuniverse.meaning: The seventh superuniverse, which contains the local universe of Nebadon and Urantia; its capital is Uversa (0:0.5, 15:14).

osiris.name: Osiris
osiris.meaning: The Egyptian god in whose judgment hall the soul of the dead was weighed for admission to bliss or consignment to hell (95:2.9).

outer-space.name: espacio exterior
outer-space.meaning: The space levels beyond the seven superuniverses, where uninhabited universes now mobilize (0:0.6, 12:1, 12:2.4).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the astronaut sense "space beyond Earth's atmosphere".
Means "later" more than "farther".

pacific-ocean.name: océano Pacífico
pacific-ocean.meaning: The ocean that formed from the early world ocean and once covered nine tenths of the earth's surface (57:8.20, 57:8.21).

palestine.name: Palestina
palestine.meaning: The land of the eastern Mediterranean where Jesus lived.

paradise.name: Paraíso
paradise.meaning: The stationary Isle at the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (0:0.5, 11:0.1).

rejected.reason: Lowercase reads as the general idea of heaven or the garden; the papers mean a specific place.

paradise-arrivals.name: Llegados al Paraíso
paradise-arrivals.meaning: The seventh stage of ascending mortals: those who reach Paradise with residential status, begin the course in divinity and absonity, and are to be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality (30:4.31).

rejected.reason: "llegadas" as a noun is the act of arrival, not the persons who arrive.
Adds "newly", which the English does not say.

paradise-central-shining.name: Resplandor Central del Paraíso
paradise-central-shining.meaning: The central shining of the spiritual glory of the Universal Father and the eternal Deities at the center of Paradise, with which a servital can have "personal contact" (11:1.3, 13:0.3, 24:7.2); the papers do not say if it is a being or a manifestation.

rejected.reason: "brillo" is ordinary gloss or shine of a surface; too small for divine glory.
The English says "Shining", not "Light"; also near "luminosidad espiritual" already in the glossary.

paradise-citizens.name: Ciudadanos del Paraíso
paradise-citizens.meaning: Native resident beings of Paradise, of more than three thousand orders, who are not directly concerned with the ascent of will creatures (30:1, 11:2.11).

rejected.reason: Loses the status sense of "citizens".

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Ciudadanos": Spanish requires a gender; the masculine plural is the neutral generic for a mixed or sexless group.

paradise-companions.name: Compañeros del Paraíso
paradise-companions.meaning: A composite group of angels drawn from several seraphic and supernaphic orders, assigned to keep company with beings, chiefly ascendant mortals, who arrive alone on Paradise (25:8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an escort or attendant role, weaker than companionship.

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Compañeros": Spanish requires a gender; the group is mixed angels, so the generic masculine plural is the neutral form.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
aliases: Cuerpos de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
paradise-corps-of-the-finality.meaning: The general name for the seven finality corps mustered on Paradise, of which the Corps of Trinitized Finaliters is one (22:8.6, 26:11.2, 31:10.20).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Finalidad del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Closer to the English 'Finality', but the done term 'Corps of the Finality' is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'; rule 4 requires that form.
That form is kept for 'Corps of Paradise Finaliters', one specific corps (31:10.3); the general name must differ.

Because 'Corps of the Finality' became 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios', the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and the specific 'Corps of Paradise Finaliters' differ in Spanish only by the article 'los'. 'Cuerpo de la Finalidad' for the done term would keep the two apart.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.note: Near-collision with corps-of-paradise-finaliters. A reviewer must decide whether to revisit 'Corps of the Finality: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

paradise-creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores del Paraíso
paradise-creator-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons (Michaels), who originate on Paradise from the Father and the Son and go out to make and rule local universes (21:0.1, 5:3.6).

paradise-deities.name: Deidades del Paraíso
paradise-deities.meaning: The three existential Deities of Paradise: the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit (0:4.9, 0:12.12).

rejected.reason: Suggests polytheism; the English uses "Deities", already "Deidad" in the glossary.

paradise-energy.name: energía del Paraíso
paradise-energy.meaning: Energy that takes origin from, or is grasped by, the Isle of Paradise, the source of all cosmic force and the center of absolute gravity (11:8, 105:3.4).

rejected.reason: "paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-force-organizers.name: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso
paradise-force-organizers.meaning: The Master Force Organizers of Paradise origin, who transmute space potency into primordial force and evolve it into the primary and secondary energies of physical reality (15:4.2, 12:2.4).

rejected.reason: Kept in line with "Directores del Poder del Universo", which uses the article.
The plural turns the cosmic force into a list of forces.

paradise-gravity.name: gravedad del Paraíso
paradise-gravity.meaning: The absolute, circular gravity grasp of the Isle of Paradise on all physical energy and matter of the master universe (11:8, 12:3, 42:2.12).

rejected.reason: Correct physics but less common; "gravedad" is the plain term in the sciences across Spanish countries.
The reader must not bring the sense "seriousness".

paradise-havona-system.name: sistema Paraíso-Havona
paradise-havona-system.meaning: The eternal central aggregation of Paradise, its satellites, and the Havona spheres, which forms the nucleus around which the superuniverses and outer space revolve (12:1, 14:1).

rejected.reason: Loses the compound name that the English hyphen makes.

paradise-havona-trinitized-sons.name: Hijos trinitizados por seres del Paraíso y Havona
paradise-havona-trinitized-sons.meaning: Sons trinitized by Paradise citizens and Havona natives acting together, held in reserve for future universe ages (22:7.8 context, 31:9).

rejected.reason: Calque of the English compound; not readable Spanish.

forcedChoices: spell out 'por seres del Paraíso y Havona': Spanish cannot stack the compound modifier; the short alias 'Hijos trinitizados Paraíso-Havona' is offered for tight sentences.

paradise-incarnation-commission.name: comisión de encarnación del Paraíso
paradise-incarnation-commission.meaning: A commission of seven unidentified Paradise personalities who arrived at the tomb before Jesus' morontia resurrection on April 9, A.D. 30 (189:1.1).

rejected.form: comisión del Paraíso para la encarnación
rejected.reason: Closes the English: it decides that the commission is from Paradise and exists for the incarnation.
"paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-master-spirits.name: Espíritus Maestros del Paraíso
paradise-master-spirits.meaning: The Seven Master Spirits of Paradise, who express the combinations of the three Paradise Deities (16:0.1, 16:1.1).

paradise-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios del Paraíso
paradise-sons-of-god.meaning: The Sons of God of Paradise origin: Creator Sons, Magisterial Sons, and Trinity Teacher Sons (20:0.1, 35:0.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'Sons of God's Paradise'.
'Paradisíaco' reads as 'idyllic'.

paradise-source-and-center.name: Fuente y Centro del Paraíso
paradise-source-and-center.meaning: The eternal Isle of Paradise as the second nondeity pattern among the Seven Absolutes of Infinity, the absolute of patterns and the foundation of gravity control (105:3.4); the packet summary ("the Universal Father") is not what 105:3.4 says, although 19:1.12 uses the phrase more broadly.

rejected.reason: The English uses "and", not a hyphen.
"paradisíaco" means "delightful" in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-trinity.name: Trinidad del Paraíso
paradise-trinity.meaning: The eternal union of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit (10:0.1, 15:0.1).

rejected.reason: The adjective reads as 'idyllic' in common use.

patmos-isle-of.name: Patmos, isla de
patmos-isle-of.meaning: Index form of the island where the apostle John was banished for four years and wrote the Book of Revelation (historical place).

rejected.reason: Kept in line with "isla de Patmos"; the generic noun stays lowercase.

paul.name: Pablo
paul.meaning: Paul of Tarsus, missionary to the gentiles and founder of much of early Christian theology (194:4.0, 196:2.1).

pella.name: Pella
pella.meaning: The place by the Jordan where John baptized Jesus and where Jesus later had a camp in Perea.
pella.note: Meaning taken from the packet summary; I did not open a paragraph for it.

pentecost-bestowal-of-spirit-of-truth.name: Pentecostés (otorgamiento del Espíritu de la Verdad)
pentecost-bestowal-of-spirit-of-truth.meaning: The day on which the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all flesh after Jesus' ascension, which transformed the apostles and the believers (Paper 194, 194:2.17, 34:5.5).

rejected.form: Pentecostés (donación del Espíritu de la Verdad)
rejected.reason: 'Donación' reads as a charitable or legal donation; 'otorgamiento' keeps the sense of a gift that is conferred.

rejected.form: Pentecostés (efusión del Espíritu de la Verdad)
rejected.reason: Translates 'outpouring', not 'bestowal'; it is a different English word in the papers.

perfection.name: perfección
perfection.meaning: The state of being complete in divine quality, existential in Paradise-Havona and experiential (attained by growth) for evolutionary creatures; the papers contrast the perfect, the perfected, and the perfecting (32:3.14, 56:4.3, 106:1.1).

rejected.reason: Means fullness, not the quality of being perfect; breaks the family perfect/perfected/perfecting.
Ordinary sense is a psychological trait; the reader must not bring that sense to 'perfección'.

perfections-of-days.name: Perfecciones de Días
perfections-of-days.meaning: The 210 Trinity personalities who rule the ten major sectors of each superuniverse as personal vicegerents of the Ancients of Days (18:4.1, 18:5.4).

perfectors-of-wisdom.name: Perfeccionadores de la Sabiduría
perfectors-of-wisdom.meaning: Trinity-created beings who personify the wisdom of divinity in the superuniverses and counsel the Ancients of Days (19:2.1).

rejected.reason: says they are perfect, not that they bring wisdom to perfection
'perfeccionista' is a personal trait

personal-aids-of-the-infinite-spirit.name: Auxiliares Personales del Espíritu Infinito
personal-aids-of-the-infinite-spirit.meaning: Beings, numbered in trillions, who serve only the Paradise presence of the Infinite Spirit and flash through the universes to execute his bidding, without a discoverable personality form (Paper 24, 24:4).

rejected.reason: 'Ayudantes' is already the fixed form for 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente); using it here would merge two different English words.
Reads as an office job title (personal assistant).

personality.name: personalidad
personality.meaning: The unique gift of the Universal Father, the one changeless reality in creature experience, which unifies body, mind, spirit, and soul without being any of them (0:5.11, 0:5.4, 1:5.13).

rejected.reason: 'Person' is a different English word in the papers.

rejected.form: (ordinary sense) personalidad = 'character traits, temperament' or 'a celebrity'
rejected.reason: The reader must not read it as psychological character or as 'a famous person'; it is a bestowed reality.

personalized-adjusters.name: Ajustadores Personalizados
personalized-adjusters.meaning: Thought Adjusters who have received personality from the Father, usually after indwelling an incarnated Paradise Son or after unusual service (Paper 109, Paper 136).

rejected.reason: Loses the sense of an act of personalization.
The reader must not read it as 'custom-made'; it means 'given personality'.

pharisees.name: fariseos
pharisees.meaning: The Jewish sect of strict observers of the law and tradition who often opposed Jesus (137:7.5).

philadelphia.name: Filadelfia
philadelphia.meaning: The city in Perea where Abner led the believers (Paper 166, 171).

philip-apostle.name: Felipe (apóstol)
philip-apostle.meaning: Philip, one of the twelve apostles and their steward, who invited others with 'Come and see' (139:5.1).

philistines.name: filisteos
philistines.meaning: The coastal people of Palestine who fought the Hebrews and defeated Saul (97:9.5, 97:9.13).

rejected.reason: Spanish has this figurative sense too; the context makes the people clear.

philo-of-alexandria.name: Filón de Alejandría
philo-of-alexandria.meaning: The Jewish philosopher of Alexandria whose religious experience, with that of Jesus and Paul, shaped early Christian doctrine (5:4.14).

phoenicians.name: fenicios
phoenicians.meaning: The ancient seafaring Semitic people of the Mediterranean coast north of Palestine.

planetary-helper-seraphim.name: serafines asistentes planetarios
planetary-helper-seraphim.meaning: The fifth order of seraphim, who come with the Planetary Adams and help the material uplift of the races (39:5.1).

rejected.reason: 'ayudante' is already 'adjutant' (espíritus ayudantes de la mente)
'Auxiliares' is already 'Aids' (Auxiliares Personales)

planetary-prince-of-urantia.name: Príncipe Planetario de Urantia
planetary-prince-of-urantia.meaning: The title first held by Caligastia; after Jesus defeated him on Mount Hermon, the title passed to Jesus (Christ Michael), with Machiventa Melchizedek a possible vicegerent (136:3.1, 93:10.6).

planetary-princes.name: Príncipes Planetarios
planetary-princes.meaning: Secondary Lanonandek Sons who rule the evolutionary worlds in the early ages (35:9.1, 50:1.1).

rejected.reason: longer; the English uses an adjective

planetary-sovereigns.name: Soberanos Planetarios
planetary-sovereigns.meaning: The title of a Planetary Prince after the bestowal Son proclaims his world settled in light and life (55:1.1).

planets.name: planetas
planets.meaning: Material spheres that circle suns, some of them inhabited by evolutionary mortals (15:6.11, 49:0.1).

platonism.name: platonismo
platonism.meaning: The philosophy of Plato, which with Stoic doctrine shaped Hellenized Jewish thought (121:6.3).

poles-of-space-communication.name: polos de comunicación del espacio
aliases: polo planetario de comunicación del espacio
poles-of-space-communication.meaning: The planetary place where messages over the mind circuit are received, linked to the point of spiritual polarity (62:7.2, 17:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'comunicación espacial' suggests satellite technology.

pontius-pilate.name: Poncio Pilato
pontius-pilate.meaning: Pontius Pilate, the Roman procurator of Judea who presided at the trial of Jesus and ordered his crucifixion (185:1.1).

potential.name: Potencial
